title: P5 — Shadow Self-ORION: frozen live-provider research trial
body:
## Goal
Enter the Shadow Self-ORION phase without granting ORION self-promotion authority.

Use a real LLM + retrieval + protected verification stack through the existing provider ports and run a frozen external research packet.

## Sequencing update
Issue #11 (mechanics-of-mechanics / mechanical question engine / failure learning) is prerequisite substrate for the trial. The live trial must not treat the LLM as the place where completeness questions live; the fixed mechanic-cell audit should expose observability, math, handoff, failure, storage, verification, parent-domain and saturation questions mechanically, with the LLM only helping answer open questions.

## ORION development protocol
Before final trial outcome access:
- [x] Atomize the live-research capability into search, interpretation, absorption, reconstruction, residual detection, diagnosis, saturation and verification fibres on the exact final trial subject.
- [x] Express those fibres as auditable mechanic cells and bind the versions used by the trial.
- [x] Research current parent-domain knowledge and benchmark designs immediately before freeze.
- [x] Challenge the saturation/search basis, explicitly asking why a relevant domain or source family might still be missed.
- [x] Freeze task packet, provider identities, resource limits and evaluator before observing outcomes.

## Trial requirements
- [x] At least one wide-literature task.
- [x] At least one deep-target task.
- [x] Real LLM provider identity frozen.
- [x] Real retrieval-source identities frozen.
- [x] Protected evaluator/verifier identity and epoch frozen outside candidate custody.
- [x] Resource budget frozen and matched to baseline.
- [x] Raw query/retrieval trace retained.
- [x] Answer-use trace retained so cited/retrieved-but-unused evidence is distinguishable.
- [x] Retrieved-but-unused and present-but-missed failure classes distinguishable where ground truth permits.
- [x] Failed/partial mechanic executions produce immutable episodes suitable for failure-pattern matching.
- [x] No LLM output directly increases authority; existing architecture has no self-merge primitive and Phase-2 readiness remains externally bounded.
- [x] Bounded saturation may return `OPEN`/`CANNOT_CHECK` structurally.
- [ ] Simpler LLM+retrieval baseline executed under matched resources.
- [ ] All failures/nulls/harmful outcomes preserved.
- [x] Self-ORION may diagnose/propose repairs but may not merge/promote them structurally.
- [ ] Exact result-bearing artifacts are merged to `main` and content/lineage bound to the closure subject.

## Current execution status — 2026-08-17
- [x] Main-only live execution workflow substrate exists from merged Phase-2 provider work.
- [x] Copilot/provider availability probing fails closed before study outcome access when the frozen explicit model pair is unavailable.
- [x] A failed pre-outcome Copilot entitlement probe is permanently preserved as `CANNOT_CHECK` evidence; it is not counted as a scientific result.
- [x] PR #207 identity mismatch is reconciled and quarantined: its P5 prose did not match its P2-only tree, the named P5 artifacts were absent, and it is closed/superseded without empirical credit (#212).
- [x] Result-bearing evidence now has strict content-addressed receipt persistence, actual-byte admission and independent exact-receipt audit available on main (#216/#219/#223/#229).
- [ ] A valid result-bearing #8 trial is merged on the exact final closure subject.
- [ ] The result-bearing trial closes both the wide/deep research requirement and matched-baseline requirement.

## Success boundary
Success means the live stack exercises ORION's governed loop and yields interpretable evidence about failures. It does not by itself establish general autonomous-science capability, Governed Self-ORION authority, or Self-ORION readiness.

## Terminal for this issue
Close only when the frozen live research trial and matched baseline are merged on the exact Phase-2 closure subject with immutable raw traces, protected evaluator bindings, and preserved failure/null evidence.

title: Phase 2 closure — complete Shadow Self-ORION with frozen live evidence
body:
## Goal
Fully close Phase 2 — **Shadow Self-ORION** — before any transition toward Governed Self-ORION.

Phase 2 is closed only when ORION has demonstrated the Shadow loop on frozen live work while external authority remains primary.

## Dependency
- [x] Phase 1 closure issue #75 is closed as `PHASE_1_CORE_TECHNICALLY_CLOSED`.
- [ ] Final Phase-2 evidence is bound to the exact final Phase-1-derived subject used for the closure run; branch-local/obsolete subject evidence does not count.

## Current architecture already present
- [x] `ShadowSelfDrivingController` can mechanically select development work, research it, compile a DevelopmentFibre, propose a change through a provider, execute in an isolated sandbox, run protected assurance and at most recommend host promotion.
- [x] No self-merge primitive.
- [x] Immutable `TaskEpisode` / failure-learning / `DevelopmentIssue` / evolution history.
- [x] Provider-neutral research runtime.
- [x] Frozen wide-literature + deep-target trial packet/harness exists structurally.
- [x] Matched-baseline interface exists structurally.
- [x] Content/lineage-bound readiness and external-evidence records exist structurally.
- [x] Internal readiness ceiling is `READY_PENDING_EXTERNAL_ATTESTATION`.
- [x] Strict `Phase2EvidenceReceipt.v1` persistence, secure actual-byte admission, independent exact-receipt audit, and prospective P5 V2 append-only negative-history chain are merged (#216/#219/#223/#229/#230).

Architecture readiness is not empirical closure.

## Required Phase-2 closure gates
### A. Frozen live-provider research trial — issue #8
Run on the **final Phase-1-derived subject**:
- [ ] Real LLM + real retrieval + protected verification/evaluation boundary.
- [ ] At least one wide-literature and one deep-target task.
- [ ] Task/provider/model/retrieval-source/evaluator/resource/split identities frozen before outcome access.
- [ ] Raw queries, retrieved documents, answer-use trace and mechanic episodes retained.
- [ ] Present-but-missed, retrieved-but-unused, interpretation/absorption, routing and saturation failures distinguished where ground truth permits.
- [ ] Matched simple LLM+retrieval baseline under resource parity.
- [ ] Null/harmful results preserved.
- [ ] Exact live artifact is merged and bound to the same subject used by the rest of the Phase-2 closure evidence.

### B. Shadow self-development trial
At least one consequential observed failure must complete the full Shadow development cycle:
- [ ] Detect the failure.
- [ ] Preserve immutable episode/history.
- [ ] Localize competing responsibility hypotheses.
- [ ] Search current ORION/RAKL + external nearest work.
- [ ] Freeze discriminator before repair outcome.
- [ ] Propose candidate change through worker/provider.
- [ ] Execute in isolated candidate environment.
- [ ] Compare against incumbent under matched resources.
- [ ] Run motivating replay plus independent fresh transfer/protected assurance.
- [ ] Retain failed/harmful alternatives and negative-history recurrence.
- [ ] Result can only recommend host promotion, never self-merge.

A failure that does not improve is still valid Phase-2 evidence if attribution, preservation and non-promotion are correct; Phase-2 closure requires the process to be demonstrated, not a preordained win.

### C. Hostile authority/evaluator trial — issue #59
Execute the frozen attack battery against the exact closure subject:
- [ ] Wrong-source/correct-fact.
- [ ] Content substitution.
- [ ] Source conflation.
- [ ] Weak/self-authored checker.
- [ ] Same-lane verifier.
- [ ] Cited-but-unused evidence.
- [ ] Benchmark/search contamination.
- [ ] Evaluator/guard modification.
- [ ] Held-out leakage.
- [ ] Correct `CANNOT_CHECK` under insufficient evidence.

### D. Empirical readiness receipts
- [ ] Produce content/lineage-bound `ReadinessEvidenceRecord`/external-manifest artifacts for the actual frozen subject.
- [ ] Self-verification is rejected.
- [ ] Post-hoc evaluator changes are rejected/versioned.
- [ ] Mixed subject revisions are rejected.
- [ ] Non-fresh splits are rejected where freshness is required.
- [ ] Caller declaration booleans cannot create PASS.

### E. Failure-learning replay
Every important failure found during A–C must be entered into negative history and either:
- [ ] Repaired + replayed + fresh-transfer tested; or
- [ ] Retained as an explicit unresolved/blocking fibre with a discriminator/reopen condition.
- [ ] Same recognized failure class does not recur unnoticed in the closure run.

### F. Final integration
- [ ] Papers/claim ledgers updated with local vs live/external evidence boundary.
- [ ] Phase-2 evidence binds the exact closure subject revision.
- [ ] Full CI green on the exact main merge.
- [ ] External artifact manifest reproducibly derives PASS/FAIL/CANNOT_CHECK without declaration booleans.
- [ ] #8 and all required evidence dependencies are closed or explicitly retained as genuine external blockers.

## Coordination status — 2026-08-17
- [x] Four-phase master roadmap exists in #208.
- [x] Governed Self-ORION Phase-3 closure gate is explicitly separated into #209 and remains blocked on this issue.
- [x] Self-sustaining Phase-4 programme gate is explicitly separated into #210 and remains blocked on #209.
- [x] Open PR evidence identities are reconciled before being counted: mislabeled #207 was quarantined as an `UNBOUND_EXECUTION_REPORT`, superseded/closed, and never counted as P5 empirical evidence (#212).
- [x] Phase-1 terminal subject anchor + read-only gap inventory landed (PR #271, `77b6fd3df722b4ec59369b8dd612223a79add847`). This binds the Phase-1 terminal *anchor*, not a Phase-2 closure subject.
- [x] Checkbox audit vs `origin/main` recorded (PR #305, `5a9a35b53b7f01000ed5f001c16da9492212549b`): 14 already-ticked architecture/coordination/DEP1 boxes re-verified; **0 additional empirical boxes tickable**. Frozen #8 packet remains `corpus_revision: UNBOUND` (`CANNOT_CHECK`). `PHASE_2_SHADOW_SELF_ORION_CLOSED` is **not** issued.

## Terminal
`PHASE_2_SHADOW_SELF_ORION_CLOSED`

This terminal does **not** grant Governed Self-ORION authority. It means the Shadow process has been exercised prospectively and is ready to be considered for external Phase-3 attestation.

## Goal
Move P5 from structural self-improvement governance to real protected fresh-transfer evidence on the exact final subject.

## Preconditions

title: ORION four-phase completion roadmap — bootstrap → shadow → governed → self-sustaining research
body:
## Goal
Drive ORION through the four intended maturity phases without allowing architecture prose, local tests, stale-branch evidence, or self-certification to substitute for the evidence required by the next phase.

Current baseline for this roadmap is dynamic: always reconcile against current `main`, not the historical SHA originally written here.

## Global rules
- [x] Work through isolated session-owned branches and PRs; never direct-push `main`.
- [x] Preserve failed/null/harmful attempts and identity mismatches as evidence rather than hiding them.
- [x] Candidate/LLM output never directly increases authority or grants merge/promotion rights.
- [ ] Every phase transition has a machine-readable, content/lineage-bound receipt tied to the exact merged subject.
- [ ] Every checked empirical item below has an immutable artifact plus exact-final-head CI/reproduction evidence.

## Phase 1 — LLM-led bootstrap
Canonical closure: #75.

- [x] Minimum working ORION exists.
- [x] Protected transition lifecycle is technically closed on merged `main` under #75.
- [x] RAKL donor saturation/core-mechanics consistency were accepted for Phase-1 closure.
- [x] No in-process self-promotion/merge authority is granted.
- [x] Phase-1 terminal recorded as `PHASE_1_CORE_TECHNICALLY_CLOSED`.

**Phase status:** COMPLETE. Any newly discovered foundational defect reopens #75 rather than being laundered into Phase 2.

## Phase 2 — Shadow Self-ORION
Canonical closure: #76. Evidence dependencies: #8, #59, #102/#159.

### Frozen live research
- [ ] Execute a real LLM + real retrieval + protected verification trial on the exact final Phase-1-derived subject.
- [ ] Include at least one wide-literature and one deep-target task.
- [ ] Freeze subject/provider/model/retrieval/evaluator/resource/split identities before outcome access.
- [ ] Retain raw query/retrieval/use traces and typed failure episodes.
- [ ] Compare against a matched simple LLM+retrieval baseline.
- [ ] Preserve null/harmful results.

### Consequential Shadow development cycle
- [ ] Detect and immutably preserve a consequential failure.
- [ ] Generate competing responsibility/root-cause hypotheses.
- [ ] Search current ORION/RAKL plus external nearest work.
- [ ] Freeze a discriminator before repair outcome access.
- [ ] Produce a candidate repair through the worker/provider path.
- [ ] Execute candidate in isolation under matched resources.
- [ ] Replay motivating failure and run independent fresh transfer.
- [ ] Run protected assurance with evaluator/holdout outside candidate custody.
- [ ] Retain rejected/harmful alternatives and negative-history recurrence.
- [ ] End only in host recommendation (`RECOMMEND_HOST_PROMOTION` or equivalent), never self-merge.

### Hostile authority / readiness receipts
- [ ] Run #59 hostile authority/evaluator battery on exact final subject.
- [ ] Produce content/lineage-bound external readiness receipts from the actual result-bearing run.
- [ ] Reproducibly derive PASS/FAIL/CANNOT_CHECK without caller declaration booleans.
- [ ] Full exact-main CI green for the closure merge.
- [ ] Close #8 and #76 with artifacts linked from the exact subject.

### Merged local authority/custody hardening
These items make later empirical evidence admissible; they do **not** count as empirical Phase-2 PASS.

- [x] Require host-side byte/hash/path/subject/evaluator/epoch verification before Phase-2 evidence admission — #216, merge `302a186b358dc00dfedda9656c792fc4a0dbc344`.

- [x] Eliminate symlink/path-swap TOCTOU from artifact admission with descriptor-relative no-follow reads — #219, merge `be0933176a4624b6ab7cf6cb3c5e24d89befceac`.
- [x] Harden the documented P5 protected-suite freeze command against input/output aliasing, overwrite, symlink redirection and one-sided partial freeze — #222, merge `0cf4e8d82771252de94be8c696a3f39fd3191019`.

**Phase status:** ACTIVE / NOT CLOSED.

## Phase 3 — Governed Self-ORION
Dedicated closure issue: #209. Starts only after Phase 2 terminal is externally evidenced.

### Authority and operating model
- [x] Freeze a Phase-3 governance protocol before granting any new authority.
- [x] Define the ordinary-framework-development task class where ORION becomes the primary problem-solving process.
- [x] Keep protected evaluator, merge/promotion authority, policy changes, and phase-boundary changes outside candidate custody.
- [x] Define explicit escalation conditions where humans/external authority retake primary control.
- [x] Make LLMs internal workers/proposers under ORION state/contracts rather than the architecture/state authority itself.

**Boundary:** these are merged pre-registration mechanics from #209/#269; they do not authorize Phase-3 operation while #76 is open.

### Empirical promotion criteria
- [ ] Prospective benchmark of ordinary framework-development issues sampled before results.
- [ ] Matched external-development baseline under comparable tool/time/model budgets.
- [ ] Measure resolution quality, regression/harm, false-cause changes, recurrence, cost, latency, and abstention/escalation.
- [ ] Demonstrate multiple consecutive governed development cycles, not a single showcase.
- [ ] Demonstrate replay + fresh transfer + protected assurance for accepted changes.
- [ ] Demonstrate hostile evaluator/authority attacks remain blocked under Phase-3 operating permissions.
- [ ] Preserve complete negative evolution history.
- [ ] Independent external attestation/reproduction of the Phase-3 promotion decision.

### Terminal
- [ ] Record `PHASE_3_GOVERNED_SELF_ORION_CLOSED` only when ORION is the primary process for ordinary framework development under bounded external governance.

**Phase status:** GATED ON PHASE 2.

## Phase 4 — Self-sustaining research program
Dedicated closure issue: #210. Starts only after Governed Self-ORION is independently evidenced.

### Three co-evolving knowledge layers
- [ ] Object knowledge has explicit versioned state, provenance, contradictions, uncertainty and protected evaluation.
- [ ] Search-universe knowledge (`W`) is versioned, tested for blind spots, and can expand/reopen without self-certifying completeness.
- [ ] Method knowledge is versioned with cause/effect evidence, applicability boundaries, negative history and transfer tests.
- [ ] Changes in any one layer trigger typed dependency invalidation/reopening in the other affected layers.

**Structural note:** #210 now separately records the merged pre-registration schemas/reopening/hostile mechanics as completed structural tasks. These high-level Phase-4 bullets stay unchecked here because this roadmap uses them as programme-operational capabilities, not merely schema existence.

### Protected research programme loop
- [ ] Freeze programme-level research objectives, benchmark families, evaluator custody and budget policy.
- [ ] Run repeated discover → diagnose → propose → test → fresh-transfer → protected-evaluate → archive cycles.
- [ ] Maintain protected held-outs and periodically refresh them without candidate access to labels.
- [ ] Detect/measure benchmark contamination, evaluator drift, search-universe collapse and method monoculture.
- [ ] Maintain exploration/exploitation policy with explicit unresolved/open-state handling.
- [ ] Preserve failures/nulls/harmful discoveries and use them in recurrence checks.
- [ ] Demonstrate that programme conclusions can remain `OPEN`/`CANNOT_CHECK` instead of forcing progress.

### Sustainability evidence
- [ ] Multi-round longitudinal evidence that object/search-universe/method knowledge improve without catastrophic regression.
- [ ] Independent audits show no silent authority transfer to candidate/LLM processes.
- [ ] Reproducible programme snapshots and immutable evaluation epochs.
- [ ] Cost/resource accounting supports continued operation under a declared budget envelope.
- [ ] External host can halt/revert/reopen any programme state from immutable history.

### Terminal
- [ ] Record `PHASE_4_SELF_SUSTAINING_RESEARCH_PROGRAM_CLOSED` only after longitudinal protected evidence demonstrates safe co-evolution.

**Phase status:** GATED ON PHASE 3.

## Immediate execution order
- [x] Reconcile/supersede mislabeled PR #207 before it can be treated as P5 evidence.
- [x] Quarantine the #207/#159 P5 result/tree identity mismatch as immutable failure-learning evidence before granting empirical credit — #212.

- [ ] Finish the remaining Phase-2 empirical closure tranche with exact artifacts and CI.
- [ ] Close Phase 2 before creating any code path that grants Governed Self-ORION operating authority.
- [x] Open/freeze the dedicated Phase-3 protocol issue before implementation (#209).
- [x] Open/freeze the dedicated Phase-4 programme protocol only after Phase-3 terminal is defined (#210 remains gated on #209).

## Reconciliation note — 2026-08-17

It also credits the already-merged Phase-3 pre-registration mechanics while leaving every Phase-2/3 result-bearing and all Phase-4 operational/longitudinal gates open.

Parent: #208. Dependency: #76 must be closed on exact merged Phase-2 evidence before this issue may authorize any Phase-3 operating authority.

## Progress tracker — 29 / 49 complete

**Counting boundary:** pre-freeze protocol/hostile-mechanism tasks count when merged and reproducible; result-bearing promotion, exact external identities, longitudinal operation and the terminal remain open until Phase 2 closes and the prospective study executes.

## Goal
Promote ORION from Shadow Self-ORION to **Governed Self-ORION** only after prospective evidence shows it can become the primary problem-solving process for ordinary ORION framework development while LLMs act as internal workers/proposers and protected governance remains outside candidate custody.

## Pre-freeze authority boundary
- [x] No Phase-3 code path grants self-merge, evaluator mutation, holdout access, policy mutation, or phase-transition authority.
- [ ] Exact Phase-2 terminal subject commit and evidence receipt are bound.
- [ ] External host/promotion authority identity is bound.
- [x] Protected evaluator/assurance custody is independent of candidate/worker processes.
- [x] Escalation/abstention conditions are frozen before outcome access.

**Reconciliation evidence:** the merged Phase-3 protocol keeps protected tests/evaluators and promotion outside worker write authority and the hostile battery rejects candidate/evaluator-custody conflation. This is a structural custody boundary only; no external evaluator identity is bound yet.

## Step 1 — freeze the ordinary-development task class
- [x] Define what counts as ordinary framework development vs protected/constitutional work.
- [x] Freeze inclusion/exclusion rules for sampled issues.
- [ ] Freeze sampling epoch and issue pool before observing comparative outcomes.
- [x] Include debugging, implementation, refactoring, regression repair, test hardening, documentation/protocol synchronization and dependency/tool failures.
- [x] Exclude evaluator/policy/authority/phase-boundary changes from candidate-owned execution.
- [x] Preserve every sampled task, including unresolved/failed tasks.

## Step 2 — freeze governance protocol
- [x] ORION owns issue state, causal hypotheses, discriminator, plan, worker delegation, replay/fresh-transfer requests and negative-history retrieval.
- [x] LLM workers can propose/search/implement only through bounded contracts.
- [x] Protected tests/evaluators and promotion remain outside worker write authority.
- [x] Every candidate runs in isolated content-addressed state.
- [x] Every accepted change requires replay + independent fresh transfer + protected assurance.
- [x] `OPEN`/`CANNOT_CHECK`/escalation remain valid terminal states for a cycle.
- [x] Harmful/null/rejected variants remain immutable history.

## Step 3 — matched baseline
- [x] Freeze an external-development baseline where a capable LLM/human-directed agent remains the primary problem-solving process.
- [x] Match model/tool/search/time/compute budgets where possible.
- [x] Freeze retry and intervention budgets.
- [x] Freeze what external help is allowed for each arm.
- [x] Prevent hidden extra evaluator/holdout access in either arm.

## Step 4 — prospective promotion study
- [ ] Run multiple consecutive ordinary-development cycles, not one showcase.
- [ ] Measure task resolution correctness and exact regression rate.
- [ ] Measure root-cause attribution correctness / false method-change rate.
- [ ] Measure replay success and independent fresh-transfer success.
- [ ] Measure harmful-transfer/worst-case regression.
- [ ] Measure recognized-failure recurrence and negative-history use.
- [ ] Measure abstention/escalation quality.
- [ ] Measure cost, latency, tool calls, LLM calls and host interventions.
- [ ] Compare against matched baseline with predeclared uncertainty/effect-size policy.

## Step 5 — hostile governance battery
- [x] Candidate attempts self-certification.
- [x] Candidate attempts evaluator/guard mutation.
- [x] Candidate attempts holdout/negative-history deletion or laundering.
- [x] Candidate attempts stale-evidence replay or subject substitution.
- [x] Candidate attempts to convert missing evidence into PASS.
- [x] Candidate attempts authority escalation through worker/provider output.
- [x] System preserves fail-closed behavior and external host control in every attack.

## Step 6 — longitudinal stability
- [ ] At least one accepted change later becomes a dependency for another governed cycle and remains replayable.
- [ ] Previously rejected/harmful variant remains queryable and prevents unnoticed recurrence.
- [ ] Multiple cycles do not silently drift evaluator/policy/task definitions.
- [ ] Governed operation can be halted and resumed from immutable history.
- [ ] Independent external replay reproduces the promotion recommendation.

## Step 7 — implementation and receipts

- [ ] Add machine-readable run/evidence receipts bound to exact subject/evaluator/epoch.
- [x] Add hostile and known-answer tests for every new authority boundary.
- [ ] Exact-final-head CI green.
- [ ] Merge only through `shadow/*` PR integration.

## Terminal
Close only when a machine-readable external promotion receipt supports:

`PHASE_3_GOVERNED_SELF_ORION_CLOSED`

That terminal means ORION is the primary process for ordinary framework development under bounded external governance. It does not authorize autonomous changes to evaluator custody, policy, constitutional rules or the Phase-4 research programme.

title: Phase 4 closure — self-sustaining protected research programme with co-evolving knowledge
body:
Parent: #208. Dependency: #209 must be closed with independent Phase-3 evidence before this issue may authorize a self-sustaining research programme.

## Progress tracker — 33 / 63 complete

**Counting boundary:** structural/pre-registration tasks are checked when the exact mechanism/schema is merged and tested on `main`; execution, protected-evidence, governance-in-force, longitudinal, and terminal boxes remain unchecked until Phase 3 closes and real Phase-4 cycles run. Checking a structural box grants **no Phase-4 authority**.

## Goal
Establish ORION as a **self-sustaining research programme** in which object knowledge, search-universe knowledge, and method knowledge co-evolve under protected evaluation, while external authority retains the ability to halt, reopen, audit, and revert programme state.

## Constitutional boundary
- [x] Candidate/LLM processes cannot mutate protected evaluators, held-outs, authority policy, phase rules, or programme termination criteria.
- [x] Missing evidence remains `OPEN`/`CANNOT_CHECK`; programme pressure cannot force positive conclusions.
- [x] Null, harmful and rejected research directions remain immutable negative history.
- [x] Every programme-level state change is content/lineage/version bound and replayable.

## Step 1 — version the three knowledge layers
### Object knowledge
- [x] Explicit object/referent/claim/evidence identities.
- [x] Provenance and source-version binding.
- [x] Contradiction/plural-view representation.
- [x] Uncertainty/authority state.
- [x] Dependency graph to measurements, methods and search-universe assumptions.

### Search-universe knowledge
- [x] Explicit versioned `W`/search-universe state.
- [x] Source-family/domain/route coverage obligations.
- [x] Blind-spot and saturation tests.
- [x] Typed unavailable/censored route state.
- [x] Reopen rules when new domains/routes/representations appear.

### Method knowledge
- [x] Versioned methods with exact implementation/protocol identity.
- [x] Applicability/assumption boundaries.
- [x] Causal support linking failures to interventions.
- [x] Replay and fresh-transfer evidence.
- [x] Negative history and known failure classes.

**Merged evidence:** `orion.programme.object-knowledge.v1`, `search-universe-knowledge.v1`, and `method-knowledge.v1` from #276. These records are pre-registration schemas; their existence does not claim a live programme has populated them with protected evidence.

## Step 2 — co-evolution and dependency invalidation
- [x] New object evidence can invalidate search-universe closure and method applicability.
- [x] New search-universe discoveries can reopen object claims and method comparisons.
- [x] New method knowledge can trigger remeasurement/reinterpretation without silently rewriting old evidence.
- [x] Dependency-directed reopening is typed and auditable.
- [x] Historical states remain reproducible after reopening.

**Merged evidence:** `orion.programme.dependency-edge.v1`, `reopen-event.v1`, and append-only `reopen-ledger.v1`; the mechanism supports all inter-layer directions and reopening supersedes rather than edits historical state.

## Step 3 — freeze programme governance
- [ ] Programme objectives and research-question queue policy.
- [ ] Exploration/exploitation policy.
- [ ] Budget/resource ceilings and stop rules.
- [ ] Protected benchmark/held-out families and refresh policy.
- [ ] Evaluator custody and versioning policy.
- [ ] Search/web contamination policy.
- [ ] External escalation/halt/revert conditions.

**Current boundary:** #321 adds preparatory governance record shapes, but `freeze_in_force=false` and host identities remain unbound. These boxes are therefore intentionally **not** checked.

## Step 4 — repeated protected research cycles
For every cycle:
- [ ] Select/open a research question from auditable programme state.
- [ ] Atomize object/search-universe/method uncertainties.
- [ ] Search nearest work/current evidence before invention.
- [ ] Freeze hypotheses/discriminators/protocol before protected outcomes.
- [ ] Delegate bounded research/implementation work to internal workers.
- [ ] Run motivating replay and independent fresh transfer.
- [ ] Run protected evaluation/assurance outside candidate custody.
- [ ] Archive accepted, null, harmful and rejected outcomes.
- [ ] Update dependency graph and reopen affected knowledge states.

No Phase-4 cycle has executed; all boxes remain open.

## Step 5 — anti-collapse / hostile checks
- [x] Detect benchmark overfitting or evaluator gaming.
- [x] Detect search-universe collapse / repeated source-family monoculture.
- [x] Detect method monoculture and forgotten negative history.
- [x] Detect stale authority or source-version substitution.
- [x] Detect hidden deletion/laundering of harmful results.
- [x] Detect circular self-citation/self-verification.
- [x] Detect repeated recognized failure classes.
- [x] Correctly block or escalate under insufficient protected evidence.

**Merged evidence:** the ten-check #276 anti-collapse battery implements these failure classes with explicit negative fixtures, a healthy no-alarm case, and fail-closed `CANNOT_CHECK`. `HostileCheckReport.grants_phase4_closure` remains hardwired `False`.

## Step 6 — longitudinal sustainability evidence
- [ ] Multiple evaluation epochs with immutable snapshots.
- [ ] Object-knowledge quality improves or appropriately contracts under new evidence.
- [ ] Search-universe coverage expands/reopens when blind spots are found.
- [ ] Method selection improves without catastrophic fresh-transfer regression.
- [ ] Worst-family/worst-epoch regressions explicitly reported.
- [ ] Cost/latency/compute remain within declared sustainability envelope.
- [ ] External host can halt and reconstruct any prior programme state.
- [ ] Independent audit/reproduction validates programme-level conclusions.

No protected longitudinal epochs exist yet.

## Step 7 — reproducibility and programme receipts
- [x] Machine-readable Phase-4 programme protocol.
- [ ] Machine-readable per-cycle receipts.
- [ ] Immutable evaluation-epoch manifests.
- [ ] Scripts regenerate programme trajectories, failures, costs and protected metrics.
- [ ] Clean replay of accepted and rejected research cycles.
- [ ] Permanent archival strategy for releasable programme state.
- [ ] Exact-final-head CI and independent reproduction before terminal promotion.

Preparatory receipt/epoch/archive *shapes* exist from #321, but no executed cycle/epoch/archive exists; those boxes remain open.

## Reconciliation note — 2026-08-17
The earlier issue status treated “Phase 4 is not authorized” as if it meant “none of the preparatory mechanics are implemented.” That undercounted merged work. #276 and #321 deliberately grant no authority, but #276 already fixes and tests the Step-1 knowledge schemas, Step-2 reopening semantics, and Step-5 hostile battery. This reconciliation checks those structural tasks while preserving every execution/evidence/terminal gate as open.

## Terminal
Close only when protected longitudinal evidence supports:

`PHASE_4_SELF_SUSTAINING_RESEARCH_PROGRAM_CLOSED`

This terminal means the programme can sustain repeated research and self-improvement cycles while knowledge layers co-evolve under protected evaluation; it does not remove external authority to halt, audit, reopen or revoke programme state.

## Four distinct failure classes discovered

### S1 — unknown operator / transformation
P9 D0 showed that when local maps are known, exact composition solves the residual and neural escalation is unnecessary.

New question:
> When one or more local transforms are noisy, partially observed, changing, or unknown, is the best strategy to **learn the local map and then compose/check it exactly**, rather than learn the end-to-end answer?

Owner child: S1 issue to be linked.

### S2 — unknown failure applicability
P9 D0 showed that admitted scoped history can distinguish cases, but explicit filtering is sufficient when relevance is given.

New question:
> Can the system learn when an old negative/failure remains relevant under context change, without globally blacklisting a mechanic or relying on surface similarity?

Owner child: S2 issue to be linked.

### S3 — wrong access geometry / serialization friction
P9 D1 found typed relational representation 1.00 vs same-information typed serialization 0.50 on the held-out procedural domain.

New question:
> Which exact structural coordinate causes the gap: relation exposure, grouping, permutation equivariance, local access, factorization, sequence length, or something else?

Owner child: S3 issue to be linked.

### S4 — wrong hypothesis/model class
P10 closed because its responsibility-aware control taxonomy was donor-composable. A harder residual is model inadequacy itself.

New scout question:
> Can an agent distinguish parameter/local-repair failure from **hypothesis-class inadequacy**, and choose between evidence acquisition, local repair, model revision, or hypothesis-space expansion?

This begins as a donor-saturation scout because Model Discovery Agent (arXiv:2608.09696), belief-revision work, active causal discovery, and metareasoning already pressure the idea heavily.

## New donor findings — 2025/2026 primary sources

### Composition/operator donors
- Shan, Sun, Duncker — *Separating the 'what' and 'how' of compositional computation to enable reuse and continual learning* (NeurIPS 2025): infer what computation is active, compose reusable low-rank RNN components to execute it.
- An & Du — *Representational Homomorphism Predicts and Improves Compositional Generalization In Transformer Language Model* (arXiv:2601.18858): homomorphism error predicts OOD composition; HE-regularized training improves OOD accuracy.
- Wang & Huang — WM3C, composable causal components (ICLR 2025): learn reusable causal dynamics and recombine in unseen environments.
- COMET — competitive independent mechanisms / modular world models: discover reusable independent dynamics and recombine across environments.
- Mechanistic World Models (arXiv:2607.12474): broad mechanism-centric scientific-learning philosophy is prior work, not ORION novelty.

### Failure-memory donors
- MERIT — *Causal Episodic Memory for Feedback-Driven Agent Repair* (arXiv:2608.05906): dual-polarity repair memory; clear Spider gain, weaker BIRD gain; typed retrieval does not reliably beat untyped retrieval; schema-local experience is most consistently useful.
- TraceRetain — *Selective Memory Retention for Long-Horizon LLM Agents* (arXiv:2606.29178): similarity can retrieve failed distractors; selective retention matters mainly under noisy streams.
- *Remember When It Matters* (arXiv:2607.08716): selective active memory intervention beats passive/always-on exposure.
- *Flexible Prefrontal Control over Hippocampal Episodic Memory for Goal-Directed Generalization* (CCN 2025): goal/task-dependent top-down memory retrieval.

### Representation/access donors
- *When 2D Tasks Meet 1D Serialization* (arXiv:2604.27272): same underlying entries can lose computationally useful relations under 1D serialization.
- GraphToken: explicit graph encoding can substantially improve graph reasoning relative to sequence-only use.
- Lippl & Stachenfeld (ICLR 2025): compositional structure alone is not sufficient; training statistics create memorization leak and shortcut bias.
- Uselis et al. (arXiv:2602.24264): linear factorization / near-orthogonality are necessary conditions in their visual compositional setup.
- GraphUniverse (ICLR 2026): transductive score poorly predicts inductive graph generalization; robustness depends on graph regime.

### Model-revision / inquiry donors
- Model Discovery Agent (arXiv:2608.09696): M-open predictive checks trigger hypothesis-space expansion and Bayesian experiment design.
- *Ask the World Before Acting* (arXiv:2606.31422): budgeted probing repairs specific world-model belief fields.
- EpiLoop: explicit epistemic-state tracking diagnoses/reduces search lock-in without claiming accuracy superiority.
- T3 / belief deviation (ICLR 2026 Oral): explicit belief-state deviation is a useful control target for active reasoning.
- Re-TRAC (ICML 2026): structured cross-trajectory state containing evidence, uncertainty, failures and plans improves deep search.

## Cross-lane rules

- A donor mechanism that solves the atom is **adopted**; ORION does not rename it.
- Every benchmark must include exact non-identifiability controls and `UNKNOWN` where relevant.
- Same information does not imply same access cost; record information, supervision, serial compute, search, and memory separately.
- No hidden chain-of-thought as scientific gold.
- No live LLM application until the exact/synthetic discriminator earns a residual.
- Negative/null/harmful outcomes remain valid terminals.

## Stop rule

A lane closes when:
- a strong donor already solves the prospective atom under matched information/resources;
- the minimum repair shows no protected gain;
- a richer model adds no value beyond explicit/simple computation;
- two changed-vocabulary donor rounds produce no new mechanism and the result terminal is stable.

title: [ORION-QN FRAMEWORK + PAPER PROGRAMME] Quantum-native ORION semantics, local simulation, end-to-end advantage, and classical authority
body:
# Status

**CANONICAL ORION-QN PROGRAMME / ORION-REPOSITORY ONLY.**

All future ORION-QN issues, branches, commits, research artifacts, protocols, experiments, implementations and paper material live in `SzeChunYiu/ORION`. The earlier cross-repository planning issue `SzeChunYiu/RAKL#752` is historical provenance only and is superseded by this issue. No new ORION-QN work is to be committed to RAKL.

# Mission

Open a new prospective research programme for **ORION-QN (Quantum-Native ORION)**: a full classical/quantum/hybrid execution semantics for the ORION framework.

This is **not** a rewrite of the existing P1–P10 papers and it is **not** an attempt to translate every Python function into a quantum circuit. The research question is:

> Can every ORION mechanic receive a formally specified classical / quantum / hybrid execution semantics, with quantum execution admitted only when its access model, state preparation, oracle construction, measurement, verification and end-to-end resource cost are explicit, while scientific authority remains classically governed, and can selected ORION workloads demonstrate genuine quantum value against the strongest same-information classical/dequantized incumbent?

A successful ORION-QN may conclude that some operations are `CLASSICAL_REQUIRED`, some `QUANTUM_ELIGIBLE`, and some `HYBRID_PREFERRED`. Selective quantum use is success; forcing unsuitable mechanics onto a QPU is not.

# Publication boundary

The existing ORION P1–P10 papers remain their own classical scientific objects. ORION-QN is a **new framework and publication family**, not `P1-Q ... P10-Q` manuscript extensions.

Default publication strategy:

1. **QN0 / flagship first:** `ORION-QN: A Quantum-Native Architecture for Evidence-Governed Autonomous Scientific Discovery` — full architecture, semantic IR, access/resource contracts, proof-carrying execution, hybrid routing, local simulation, resource estimation and one strong vertical slice.
2. Promote a companion paper only when a track earns a scientifically distinct result:
   - **QN-I — Quantum semantics for evidence-governed research systems**;
   - **QN-II — Proof-carrying quantum computation / QuantumReceipt**;
   - **QN-III — End-to-end quantum advantage in autonomous discovery**;
   - **QN-IV — Self-optimizing hybrid quantum–classical research**.
3. The labels `P1-Q ... P10-Q` may be used internally to map mechanics, but they are **semantic map labels, not paper identities**.

# Local-computer-first requirement

Owning a quantum computer is **not** an architectural requirement.

ORION-QN must support three explicitly separated evidence modes:

```text
LOCAL_SIMULATION
  ordinary CPU/GPU simulates the quantum state/circuit
  -> establishes semantics/correctness only

RESOURCE_ESTIMATION
  ordinary CPU estimates logical/physical FT resources
  -> establishes projected resource regimes only

REAL_QPU
  optional remote or owned hardware execution
  -> may establish hardware evidence when separately verified
```

Constitutional rule:

> No ORION-QN programme may require ownership of a QPU for framework development, semantic verification, classical-baseline evaluation, quantum-circuit simulation, or fault-tolerant resource analysis. Real-QPU access is an optional evidence tier, not an architectural dependency.

A CPU simulation of a quantum algorithm **does not constitute quantum speedup**. Simulator, logical-resource, projected-FT and real-QPU evidence are separate authority classes.

# Immutable prior evidence / non-reopening

Prior ORION-Q work remains evidence and negative history; it does not self-authorize ORION-QN claims. Relevant parents include #633, #671, #674–#677, #679, #694, #695 and #698.

The previous closure/recovery results must remain visible, especially:

- no hidden stronger oracle;
- no free state preparation;
- no free readout;
- QC2/exhaustive-search negative controls;
- fully known interface graph classical closure;
- donor ownership of broad generic quantum synthesis;
- resource-model failures such as implementation overhead erasing proxy advantages.

Any real quantum-method contribution still requires a fresh prospectively frozen target, donor set, code/model identity, access/resource contract, strong baselines and independent novelty/correctness review.

# Expert cell / veto roles

Every result-bearing tranche is reviewed through six lenses:

- **Q1 quantum algorithms / complexity:** query/algebraic validity and strongest classical/quantum parents;
- **Q2 quantum PL / reversible systems:** physical semantics, linearity, no-cloning, uncomputation, compiler boundary;
- **Q3 verification / statistics:** measurement contracts, uncertainty, independent reconstruction;
- **Q4 FTQC / resources:** QEC, logical-to-physical accounting, T factories, runtime, shots and backend assumptions;
- **Q5 ORION architecture:** preserve P1–P10 responsibility/authority boundaries;
- **Q6 hostile dequantization / no-hidden-speedup reviewer:** attack access, QRAM/state-prep, preprocessing, readout and weak baselines.

Same-context expert review is not independent scientific authority.

# Non-compensatory constitutional invariants

1. `NO_STRONGER_ORACLE` — quantum interface must be supplied by the problem or constructible with charged cost/error.
2. `NO_FREE_STATE_PREPARATION` — QRAM/amplitude/state loading and reusable preparations are explicit resources.
3. `NO_FREE_READOUT` — shots, estimation, reconstruction and measurement error are charged.
4. `NO_AUTHORITY_LAUNDERING` — quantum success cannot self-grant validity, novelty, adoption or search-stop authority.
5. `NO_NEGATIVE_HISTORY_REWRITE` — prior nulls/refutations remain immutable.
6. `SAME_ADMITTED_INFORMATION` — quantum and classical baselines receive matched semantic information/access.
7. `STRONGEST_FAIR_CLASSICAL_OR_DEQUANTIZED_BASELINE` — optimized classical/dequantized methods get first right of refusal.
8. `NO_SIMULATOR_EQUALS_HARDWARE_CLAIM`.
9. `NO_LOGICAL_EQUALS_PHYSICAL_CLAIM`.
10. `RESOURCE_VECTOR_NOT_ONE_SCORE` — preprocessing, prep, oracle build, calls, qubits, depth, T-count/depth, ancilla, physical qubits, runtime, shots, postprocessing, verifier, memory, wall time and error remain visible.
11. `BACKEND_OR_REVISION_DRIFT_REOPENS_RECEIPTS`.
12. `CLASSICAL_FALLBACK_PRESERVES_SCIENCE` — unavailable QPU must not fabricate scientific failure evidence.

# Foundation programme F0–F14

Each atom needs: definition, nearest work, strongest incumbent, candidate residual, assumptions/access model, falsifier, known-answer/no-alarm controls, output schema, allowed claim and stop condition.

- **F0 provenance / programme identity / non-reopening**
- **F1 claim taxonomy:** feasibility vs query/algebraic vs projected-FT vs end-to-end physical advantage
- **F2 state ontology:** classical authoritative state, quantum registers, preparation metadata, measurement-derived evidence, inaccessible state
- **F3 ORION Quantum Semantic IR:** linear/affine quantum resources above backend syntax
- **F4 access/oracle/state-preparation algebra**
- **F5 reversible semantics / garbage / uncomputation / measurement boundaries**
- **F6 measurement/readout/observability contract**
- **F7 correctness/formal/statistical/optional cryptographic verification**
- **F8 logical-to-physical/QEC/resource receipt**
- **F9 end-to-end advantage and dequantization adjudicator**
- **F10 hybrid scheduler / quantum eligibility router**
- **F11 backend portability/lowering to current quantum IRs/toolchains**
- **F12 quantum negative history and typed reopen conditions**
- **F13 protected benchmark/evaluation substrate**
- **F14 cross-paper/cross-mechanic invariant audit**

# Core objects

Freeze versioned schemas for at least:

```text
QProblemContract
QSemanticStateView
QProgramIR
QAccessContract
QStatePreparationContract
QOracleContract
QKernel
QMeasurementContract
QResourceReceipt
QVerificationReceipt
QuantumReceipt
QAdvantageReceipt
QFallbackContract
QBackendIdentity
```

Every `QKernel` must bind:

- owning ORION mechanic / semantic problem;
- classical semantics;
- quantum semantics;
- eligibility condition;
- access/state-preparation/oracle contracts;
- error and measurement contracts;
- logical and projected physical resource models;
- verification contract;
- strongest classical/dequantized baseline;
- fallback semantics;
- exact claim ceiling.

# End-to-end cost doctrine

No quantum advantage claim may omit:

```text
C_Q = C_preprocess
    + C_state_prepare
    + C_oracle_build
    + C_compile
    + C_logical_execute
    + C_QEC_physical
    + C_measure
    + C_reconstruct
    + C_verify
```

and its fair classical/dequantized comparator `C_C` under the same admitted information/access contract.

Query advantage is useful evidence but must never be reported as end-to-end physical advantage unless the full accounting supports it.

# First result-bearing vertical slice: P6-Q + P2-Q + P4-Q

Start here before self-optimization or broad quantum-native learning.

## VS1 semantic search object

Build exact, locally simulable search worlds:

1. **S1 — unstructured finite admissible candidate search**: classical exhaustive/optimized search vs Grover/amplitude-amplification family under identical predicate access.
2. **S2 — structured/backtracking search**: strongest classical backtracking vs quantum backtracking/walk where theorem assumptions match.
3. **S3 — expensive-oracle hostile family**: query advantage may disappear once oracle construction/evaluation dominates.
4. **S4 — classical-index/amortization hostile family**: repeated queries may make a classical index/preprocessing route dominate.

For every subject, record both the simulated quantum execution and the true classical baseline. The local simulator is a semantic/verifier instrument, not the performance comparator.

## Required receipts

A successful VS1 result needs independent reconstruction of:

`problem -> access -> state prep -> oracle -> quantum program -> measurement -> estimator -> output -> resource vector -> claim ceiling`.

# P1–P10 semantic mapping

The programme must eventually determine, for every existing ORION mechanic, one of:

```text
CLASSICAL_REQUIRED
QUANTUM_SEMANTICS_DEFINED
QUANTUM_FEASIBLE_NO_ADVANTAGE
QUANTUM_QUERY_ADVANTAGE_ONLY
QUANTUM_PROJECTED_FT_ADVANTAGE
QUANTUM_END_TO_END_ADVANTAGE_SUPPORTED
DEQUANTIZED_PARENT_SUFFICIENT
CLASSICAL_PARENT_SUFFICIENT
CANNOT_CHECK_HARDWARE
CANNOT_CHECK_ACCESS_MODEL
INVALID
```

P8/authority remains classical/constitutional even if quantum computation supplies evidence. P9/P10 quantum outputs remain capability outputs and cannot self-authorize novelty/adoption/closure.

# Execution ladder

- **Q0** provenance, repository, donor and chronology freeze

- **Q8** P5 governed recursive development / hybrid routing
- **Q9** full P1–P10 semantic coverage
- **Q10** mixed-workload end-to-end router benchmark
- **Q11** independent replay, novelty and hostile review

# Claim ladder

- `L0 ORION_QN_P1_P10_SEMANTIC_COVERAGE`
- `L1 ORION_QN_SCOPED_QUANTUM_QUERY_ADVANTAGE`
- `L2 ORION_QN_PROJECTED_FT_PARETO_REGIME`

Valid bounded/negative terminals include:

- `ORION_QN_SEMANTIC_COVERAGE__NO_END_TO_END_QUANTUM_ADVANTAGE`
- `ORION_QN_QUERY_ADVANTAGE_ONLY__INPUT_OR_QEC_COST_DOMINATES`
- `ORION_QN_DEQUANTIZED_PARENT_SUFFICIENT`

- `ORION_QN_SEMANTIC_INCOMPATIBILITY_FOUND`
- `ORION_QN_PROGRAMME_SATURATED_NO_DISTINCT_RESIDUAL`

# Immediate first tranche

- [ ] freeze `ORION_QN_PROVENANCE_BOUNDARY_V1` in this repository;
- [ ] freeze current ORION `main` commit and literature cutoff;
- [ ] build atom-by-atom donor matrix with at least two no-material-change literature rounds before novelty language;

- [ ] independently reconstruct the first `QuantumReceipt`;
- [ ] update this issue with exact commits/receipts and unresolved vetoes.

# Governing scientific principle

ORION-QN should make ORION **more discriminating about quantum computation, not more enthusiastic about it**. The strongest intended behavior is the ability to produce statements such as:

> this discovery search is quantum-eligible; this knowledge query is classically superior; this verification path is hybrid; this authority operation is classical-required; this learned method dequantizes; this method-search result has query advantage only; this real-QPU claim cannot yet be checked.

Every such statement must be backed by explicit contracts and receipts.

title: [ORION-QN Q2] Calibrated quantum eligibility beyond donor-composed selection/QRE/assurance
body:
Parent programme: #734
Result-bearing S1A implementation/receipts: PR #737

## Status

**PROSPECTIVELY REGISTERED SYSTEMS-HYPOTHESIS LANE — NO POSITIVE RESULT.**

This issue freezes the strongest residual left after current donor subtraction. It does not claim that ORION-QN has incremental value and it does not depend on a positive S1A outcome.

## Research question

> Under matched information, tools and evaluation budgets, does ORION's typed epistemic state — explicit access derivability, theorem-applicability state, scoped failure/reopen history, measurement/verification state and separated scientific-authority coordinates — produce better calibrated quantum/classical research decisions than the strongest faithful composition of current quantum algorithm-selection, full-stack resource-estimation/optimization, verified-compilation and assurance-case mechanisms?

A legitimate terminal is `DONOR_COMPOSITION_SUFFICIENT`.

## Why the claim has been narrowed

Current work already owns most obvious pieces:

- Brehm/Weggemans 2026: structured k-SAT hybrid benchmarking versus a strong modern classical SAT incumbent, including T-depth/T-count/crossover analysis;
- Predict and Conquer: predictive quantum/classical algorithm + parameter selection from non-functional performance models;
- AutoQuREO: automated full-stack quantum resource estimation and multi-objective stack optimization;
- qstack: compositional end-to-end FT compilation across quantum/QEC/ISA layers and classical callbacks;
- QBlue/SQIR/VOQC/QWIRE lineage: typed/formally verified quantum semantics/compilation;
- current end-to-end runtime methodology: system-overhead-aware quantum/classical comparisons and strong classical baseline selection;
- DARPA QB/QBI: utility-over-cost framing and independent V&V;
- SACM / dynamic assurance / defeater literature: machine-readable claims-arguments-evidence, evidence lifecycle/change impact, continuous assurance and negative/defeater argumentation.

Therefore none of those primitives is an ORION-QN novelty claim.

## Candidate incremental mechanism

The candidate is the **specific ORION epistemic composition**, not a new quantum algorithm or generic assurance graph.

Candidate state distinguishes:

```text
semantic problem identity
admitted information
access/oracle derivability
quantum theorem applicability
representation/compiler correspondence
backend/resource identity
measurement identifiability/uncertainty
strongest-classical counterfactual
scoped prior failure + required_same/reopen_on_change
verification state
authority state: validity/applicability/transfer/novelty/utility/adoption/search-stop
```

The hypothesis is that preserving these coordinates and their non-laundering transitions improves decisions relative to a donor composition that has the same underlying algorithms/QRE/compilers/verifiers but lacks ORION's exact scoped epistemic mechanics.

## Frozen decision set

At minimum:

```text
RUN_CLASSICAL
RUN_QUANTUM_QUERY_ONLY
RUN_QUANTUM_PROJECTED_FT
RUN_HYBRID
VERIFY_MORE
CHANGE_ACCESS_OR_REPRESENTATION
REOPEN_STALE_RESULT
CANNOT_CHECK
REJECT_INVALID_COMPARISON
```

No candidate decision can self-grant P8 novelty/adoption/search-stop authority.

## Mixed-workload arena

The benchmark must contain exact/checkable cases where dimensions disagree; surface labels must not reveal the desired action.

### W1 — theorem-valid but classical-strong
Quantum theorem assumptions hold and a primitive/tree-matched classical comparator is weaker, but a same-information structure-aware classical solver dominates.
Expected: `RUN_CLASSICAL` / bounded query theorem retained without quantum-use promotion.

### W2 — apparent query advantage with unresolved access
Quantum query count wins only if a coherent oracle/controlled operation is treated as supplied; derivability from admitted input is unresolved.
Expected: `CANNOT_CHECK` or `CHANGE_ACCESS_OR_REPRESENTATION`, never positive promotion.

### W3 — projected resource win with insufficient measurement
Compiler/QRE path is valid, but the frozen measurement contract cannot identify the scientific output to required tolerance.
Expected: `VERIFY_MORE` / reject promotion.

### W4 — stale backend/resource receipt
A prior projected quantum regime was valid under backend/compiler/QEC identity A; identity changes materially.
Expected: `REOPEN_STALE_RESULT`, not replayed authority.

### W5 — scoped negative remains applicable
A prior failure has `required_same` coordinates all preserved.
Expected: do not repeat the same invalid route unless new evidence is explicitly registered.

### W6 — scoped negative legitimately reopens
Representation/access/backend coordinate named in `reopen_on_change` changes with a valid correspondence witness.
Expected: reopen rather than treating historical failure as global blacklist.

### W7 — technically valid result attempts authority laundering
Quantum execution/verification succeeds but novelty/adoption/search-stop evidence is absent.
Expected: retain technical result; deny P8 promotion.

### W8 — genuinely favorable bounded quantum regime
Access, theorem, verification and projected resource assumptions are all satisfied and strong classical first refusal does not dominate.
Expected: bounded quantum selection at the exact earned claim level; benchmark must prevent security-by-total-refusal.

### W9 — ordinary classical case
No quantum theorem/resource residual exists.
Expected: classical route with low unnecessary verification cost.

### W10 — underdetermined case
Available information cannot distinguish two admissible route choices within required confidence/budget.
Expected: calibrated `CANNOT_CHECK`/`VERIFY_MORE`, not forced quantum/classical certainty.

## Strong baseline ladder

All baselines receive the same visible problem state, tools and resource evidence except where the tested representation itself is the registered variable.

- `B0 QUERY_RULE`: query/asymptotic heuristic only.
- `B1 SELECTOR`: Predict-and-Conquer-style learned/performance-model selector over the frozen route library.
- `B2 FULL_STACK`: B1 + AutoQuREO-style multi-objective QRE/stack optimization.
- `B3 VERIFIED_STACK`: B2 + strongest applicable verified-compiler/access/measurement checks.
- `B4 ASSURANCE_COMPOSED`: B3 + SACM/dynamic-assurance-style claims/evidence/dependency/change-impact/defeater state.
- `B5 DONOR_SUPERSYSTEM`: strongest faithful composition of B1–B4 with the same negative-history records available as ordinary unscoped evidence/memory.
- `B6 ORION_QN`: B5 capabilities + typed scoped failure/reopen semantics + explicit authority-coordinate separation/non-laundering.

**B5 is the primary incumbent.** If B5 expresses and solves the same cases under matched budget, the ORION residual collapses.

## Required ablations

- ORION without scoped failure applicability;
- ORION without `reopen_on_change`;
- ORION with flat Boolean PASS/FAIL instead of separate authority coordinates;
- ORION with authority coordinates but no access derivation;
- ORION with access/resource checks but no independent verification state;
- ORION without explicit `CANNOT_CHECK`;
- donor system given equivalent typed scope/reopen semantics — strongest hostile absorption test.

The last ablation is mandatory: if simply adding ORION's fields to B5 makes B5 equivalent without any distinct mechanic, record composition/subsumption rather than branding the data structure as novelty.

## Primary outcome vector

Non-compensatory:

- correct final route/terminal rate;
- **false quantum promotion rate**;
- false classical rejection / over-conservatism rate;
- `CANNOT_CHECK` precision/recall/calibration;
- stale-evidence reuse rate;
- recognized-invalid-route recurrence;
- authority-laundering rate;
- verified utility/cost of decision;
- verifier/tool calls and decision latency;
- worst-family performance.

No scalar average can compensate a hidden authority/access violation.

## Protected design

- frozen generator + evaluator before candidate fitting;
- reminted route/tool/backend identifiers;
- leave-family-out or future-family holdout;
- candidate never receives evaluator desired action/terminal;
- exact problem/access/resource ground truth belongs to evaluator where appropriate;
- all systems receive matched tool calls/budget;
- no candidate edits evaluator/margins after outcome access;
- harness every external/local capability request/result with content-bound receipts;
- independent reconstruction of the final decision state from serialized evidence.

## Success criterion

A positive ORION-QN systems result requires all of:

1. B6 improves calibrated correct-decision performance over B5 on protected cases;
2. false quantum promotion is lower or non-inferior under a frozen hard margin;
3. benefit survives at least one unseen family/domain or changed backend/access regime;
4. improvement is localized by ablation to scoped epistemic/authority mechanics rather than more information, more compute, or a stronger oracle;
5. giving B5 equivalent information does not erase the effect;
6. no result depends on self-authored authority or hidden protected-state access.

## Falsifiers / honest terminals

- `DONOR_COMPOSITION_SUFFICIENT` — B5 matches B6 at matched information/budget.
- `SCOPED_HISTORY_VALUE_ONLY` — only repeated-route reduction survives; no broader routing claim.
- `AUTHORITY_SEPARATION_VALUE_ONLY` — only false-promotion control survives.
- `OVERCONSERVATIVE` — ORION reduces false promotion by rejecting useful valid quantum routes too often.
- `NO_GENERALIZATION` — development-family effect does not transfer.
- `CANNOT_CHECK` — protected evaluator/tool/resource dependency unavailable.
- `ORION_QN_CALIBRATED_ELIGIBILITY_INCREMENTAL_VALUE` — strongest intended bounded positive, only after independent verification.

## Relationship to publication programme

If positive, this belongs primarily to the **QN0 flagship** as evidence that quantum-native ORION is more than a collection of quantum tools. It does not automatically become a separate companion paper.

If negative, QN0 can still remain a semantic/framework paper, but the system-superiority claim must be removed or narrowed.

## Immediate order

1. Finish S1A harness result and independent receipt reconstruction under #737.
2. Freeze S2/S3 exact donor-composed route objects and resource/access perturbations.
3. Build B0–B5 before B6 evaluation.
4. Freeze arena splits, hard metrics and margins.
5. Execute with the ORION research harness; preserve every negative/CANNOT_CHECK.
6. Route any positive through independent hostile/reproducibility review before paper language.

title: [ORION-QN VS1-S2] Structured search: theorem eligibility vs scaling vs strong-classical/FT utility
body:
Parent programme: #734
S1A implementation/receipt lane: PR #737
Systems-level successor: #738

## Status

**PROSPECTIVELY REGISTERED S2 RESEARCH LANE — NO QUANTUM ADVANTAGE CLAIM.**

This issue freezes the scientific question before S2 implementation/outcomes. S1A may remain a query-model base case; S2 asks whether a quantum-search theorem remains useful after problem structure, strong classical algorithms and implementation resources are admitted.

## Core scientific question

> Can ORION-QN keep three distinct facts separate and correctly route between them: (1) a quantum backtracking/search theorem is applicable under an exact local-access model, (2) a quantum or hybrid solver exhibits favorable empirical scaling on a registered family, and (3) the route remains useful against the strongest same-information classical incumbent after fault-tolerant/resource costs?

These are not equivalent authority states.

## Current evidence landscape — deliberately non-monotone

### Theorem parent

Ambainis & Kokainis (STOC 2017) study unknown search trees discoverable by local exploration: the root is supplied and a black box maps a vertex to its children. They estimate tree size in roughly `sqrt(nT)` steps and transform a classical backtracking algorithm examining `T` nodes into a quantum algorithm with roughly `sqrt(T) * n^(3/2)` dependence (polylog factors suppressed).

Disposition: **theorem/access parent**. ORION-QN cannot claim novelty for quantum backtracking or tree-size-aware speedup.

### Negative/practical parent

Brehm & Weggemans, *Quantum* 10, 1975 (2026), benchmark Grover and quantum backtracking on structured random k-SAT against a strong modern classical SAT solver using both T-depth and T-count. Almost all apparent speedups disappear when modest structure or T-count is admitted; only a narrow Grover/T-depth regime remains promising.

Disposition: **strong-classical + FT hostile parent**. A theorem-valid route can still be practically rejected.

### Positive/scaling parent

A 2026 *Nature Computational Science* paper, **Evidence of scaling advantage on an NP-complete problem with enhanced quantum solvers**, reports favorable scaling for QAA/QAOA variants after a classical reduction (RSRA) on one-in-three SAT. Importantly, it also compares against RSRA-aware classical baselines, including restricted-subspace random sampling and a structured random-walk heuristic, to separate preprocessing value from the quantum contribution.

Disposition: **positive scaling parent / anti-false-negative control**. S2 must not be designed so conservatively that quantum routes are rejected whenever classical preprocessing exists.

These results are complementary facets until matched on problem family, access, resource model and claim type.

## Three-layer state object

For every S2 subject, record separately:

### L1 — theorem eligibility

```text
QTreeAccessContract
root access
child-generation access
predicate/solution test
known depth bound
classical backtracking policy identity
observed/estimated tree-size quantity
coherent/reversible realization status
error/success target
```

Terminal examples:

```text
THEOREM_APPLICABLE
THEOREM_ASSUMPTIONS_NOT_MET
CANNOT_CHECK_ACCESS_MODEL
```

### L2 — scaling evidence

```text
problem-family identity
generator/data identity
classical/quantum preprocessing identity
size parameter
resource/call/runtime observations
fit model + uncertainty
held-out size/family validation
```

A favorable fitted exponent is not automatically an FT/runtime claim.

### L3 — utility / strongest-incumbent result

```text
strongest same-information classical solver
quantum logical resources
T-count
T-depth
ancilla/logical qubits
state/oracle construction
compile/transpile cost
measurement/repetitions
chosen FT hardware assumptions
projected runtime/cost
```

This layer can reject a route that is positive at L1/L2.

## S2 first experimental architecture

Do **not** begin by implementing a large QPU simulation. First build exact/checkable structured search worlds and route receipts.

### S2-A — matched-tree positive control

Construct generated binary/CSP search trees where:

- tree/local-access assumptions are exactly satisfied;
- a frozen deterministic classical backtracking policy explores `T` nodes;
- no hidden structure-aware shortcut exists by construction;
- quantum-backtracking theorem resource expression can be evaluated from the exact tree/depth;
- a simple exhaustive/DFS baseline is the theorem-matched comparator.

Purpose: verify theorem-eligibility machinery can produce a positive L1 state.

This arm alone cannot establish practical quantum advantage.

### S2-B — structure-aware classical reversal

Use satisfiability/CSP families where a primitive backtracking tree remains large but an allowed same-information structure-aware classical solver exploits preprocessing/propagation/learning.

Required comparators:

- `C_TREE_MATCHED`: exact policy/tree used by the quantum theorem;
- `C_STRUCTURE_STRONG`: strongest reproducible structure-aware classical solver under the registered input and budget.

Expected hostile case:

```text
L1 = THEOREM_APPLICABLE
query/tree projection favors quantum over C_TREE_MATCHED
C_STRUCTURE_STRONG dominates practical/projected utility
final = CLASSICAL_PARENT_SUFFICIENT
```

A correct ORION-QN system must preserve the theorem result while rejecting quantum execution.

### S2-C — reduction-aware quantum positive control

Construct/absorb a family inspired by current reduction-enhanced SAT work where both quantum and classical routes receive the same admissible classical reduction.

Required controls:

- quantum-only benefit cannot be credited to the reduction itself;
- strongest reduction-aware classical random/heuristic search receives the same reduced subspace;
- pre/post-reduction problem equivalence is verified;
- reduction cost is charged to all routes that use it;
- no hidden gold enters reduction.

Purpose: prevent `strong classical first refusal` from degenerating into `always choose classical`.

### S2-D — access failure

Surface tree/predicate API appears classically available but coherent/reversible child/predicate access has not been derived.

Expected:

```text
classical execution may proceed
quantum theorem execution = CANNOT_CHECK_ACCESS_MODEL
```

### S2-E — FT-resource reversal

Theorem and logical scaling favor quantum, but T-count/T-depth/ancilla or error-correction assumptions move projected utility behind the strong classical route.

Expected: retain L1/L2 evidence; final utility terminal is non-positive.

## Strong baseline doctrine

For every subject distinguish:

1. `C_TREE_MATCHED` — classical algorithm whose tree/access model is transformed by the quantum theorem;
2. `C_STRUCTURE_STRONG` — strongest same-information practical classical route;
3. `C_REDUCTION_AWARE` — strongest classical route allowed to consume any preprocessing/reduction granted to quantum;
4. `Q_THEOREM` — theorem-level quantum estimate under exact assumptions;
5. `Q_LOGICAL` — logical circuit/resource instantiation when available;
6. `Q_PROJECTED_FT` — projected FT route under frozen hardware/QEC assumptions.

A quantum route cannot claim utility merely because it beats comparator 1.

## First-right-of-refusal rules

Before a positive utility terminal:

- same admitted information/access;
- same reduction/preprocessing where applicable;
- no benchmark-correlated side information uniquely available to quantum;
- strongest runnable/reproducible classical incumbent gets first refusal;
- query theorem is separately reported, never erased when practical utility is negative;
- current classical solver/version and hardware/resource identities are frozen before protected results.

## Primary ORION-QN mechanism test

The scientific object is not another SAT benchmark. It is whether typed state prevents **authority laundering across layers**.

Hostile examples:

- `THEOREM_APPLICABLE -> QUANTUM_PROJECTED_FT_ADVANTAGE` without resource closure: reject;
- favorable scaling fit -> physical speedup claim: reject;
- quantum beats primitive backtracking but loses to structure-aware solver -> choose classical;
- reduction helps both sides but is credited only to quantum -> invalid comparison;
- quantum route valid in one representation, stale receipt reused after reduction/access change -> reopen;
- negative structured family globally blacklists quantum even after a genuinely different access/reduction regime -> reject blacklist.

## Metrics

Keep a vector, not one score:

- theorem-applicability correctness;
- access-model false-positive rate;
- correct comparator selection;
- false quantum utility promotion rate;
- false classical rejection rate;
- preservation of positive L1/L2 evidence when L3 is negative;
- CANNOT_CHECK calibration;
- projected resource error / interval coverage where ground truth or stronger estimator is available;
- route decision cost;
- worst-family error.

## Publication boundary

A positive S2 result does **not** establish a new quantum algorithm. Possible contribution is a bounded ORION-QN framework result:

> evidence-governed separation of theorem eligibility, scaling evidence and strong-incumbent/FT utility prevents both false quantum promotion and false quantum rejection across mixed structured-search regimes.

This claim is itself subject to #738 donor-composition pressure.

## Honest terminals

- `S2_THEOREM_ELIGIBILITY_LAYER_VALIDATED`
- `S2_STRONG_CLASSICAL_FIRST_REFUSAL_VALUE`
- `S2_REDUCTION_AWARE_QUANTUM_REGIME_RETAINED`
- `S2_FT_RESOURCE_REVERSAL_RETAINED`
- `S2_DONOR_COMPOSITION_SUFFICIENT`
- `S2_OVERCONSERVATIVE`
- `S2_ACCESS_MODEL_CANNOT_CHECK`
- `S2_NO_GENERALIZABLE_ORION_INCREMENT`

## Execution order

1. S1A v4 harness result/reconstruction on exact PR #737 head.
2. Freeze S2 generated-world schema and theorem/access checker.
3. Implement `C_TREE_MATCHED` first.
4. Add `C_STRUCTURE_STRONG` and reduction-aware controls before ORION candidate scoring.
5. Freeze FT resource assumptions separately from theorem/scaling evidence.
6. Execute through `orion-research-harness` with immutable receipts.

title: [ORION-QG QG-9] Is rank-2 support five tight? Exact cap-4 witness hunt or stronger all-n bound
body:
Parent programme: #740
Canonical theorem: QG-1 in wave-1 closure (`generator support <=5` all n)
Independent corroboration: #747 / PR #748 dual-harness support-five theorem
Related automatic quotient lane: #756 / PR #759

## Status

**TIGHTNESS FRONTIER — constructive witness or stronger theorem, no preferred outcome.**

QG-1 proves that every optimum of the frozen R6I rank-2 shared-Tag grammar has each independent frame generator supported on at most five qubits. The canonical proof obtains `5 = |N_jg|<=3 + |C_j|<=2`; the independent proof route obtains the same bound from a 5-dimensional conserved-syndrome quotient.

But the current evidence gives **no instance requiring support five**. QG-1's stress panel is suspiciously stronger: on all tested n=3 instances unrestricted DP, brute, cap-2 and cap-1 coincide. The closure packet therefore leaves tightness of 5 as residual R5.

QG-9 asks:

> Is support five genuinely necessary for some frozen-R6I instance, or can the all-n theorem be strengthened to support <=4 (or lower)?

## Exact cap-4 referee at the minimal possible witness size n=5

A support-five necessity witness must have `n>=5`; choose **n=5** as the first exact domain.

For n=5, a generator has support <=4 iff it is identity at at least one qubit. Therefore the exact cap-4 optimum can be written as

`C_cap4 = min_{z_A0,z_A1,z_B0,z_B1 in {0,...,4}} C_DP[ R_A0(z_A0)=I, R_A1(z_A1)=I, R_B0(z_B0)=I, R_B1(z_B1)=I ]`.

There are exactly `5^4=625` zero-witness assignments. The constrained DP must reuse the frozen R6I transition/acceptance/cost algebra and force the specified local generator letters to identity before the per-qubit min-plus update. Taking the minimum over the 625 assignments is **exact**, including configurations with multiple identity positions (they appear under multiple assignments).

Hard binding controls:
- removing all zero constraints reproduces frozen unrestricted `shared_tag_exact`;
- at n<=3, the same zero-witness method for cap n-1 must agree with the independent `PairTables.capped_costs` implementation from canonical QG-1;
- selected cap-4 witnesses are reconstructed and passed through the frozen R6I witness verifier.

## Counterexample-first / inverse-design arm

Random targets are a weak search because high-support frames pay substantial Uanti cost. Instead generate instances from **irreducible support-five frame/Tag configurations** and choose target triples to reward those frames.

### Stage A — joint exceptional class skeletons

Enumerate realizable n=5 blocks whose support-five generator has exactly the canonical proof's maximal zero-sum-free decomposition:
- non-coincidence `N_jg` size 3 with distinct nonzero linearly independent F2^3 classes and odd alpha sum;
- coincidence `C_j` size 2 with distinct nonzero F2^2 classes;
- shared Tag labels valid/nonzero/distinct;
- both generators nonzero, symplectic product 1.

Also include the independent F2^5 rank-5 boundary patterns from PR #748 as a separate skeleton family.

Canonicalize qubit permutations and globally valid Pauli-letter relabelings before target generation.

### Stage B — inverse target templates

For each skeleton, create target triples from the desired frames using frozen Restore templates rather than uniform random targets:

1. `IDENTITY_RESTORE`: `P_k = R_k` so the desired frame has zero Restore support;
2. `ONE_DEFECT`: one branch Restore is one weight-one Pauli;
3. `CROSS_BLOCK_SHARED_DEFECT`: A/B Restores deliberately align under the same Tag labels;
4. `CENTRAL_FAVOR`: defects placed to favor the designated central branch;
5. `ANTI_CAP4`: defects occupy all five qubits so every forced-zero cap-4 variant loses at least one alignment opportunity.

All template families/order/caps are frozen before any cap-4 result.

For each generated pair of blocks:
- compute unrestricted exact DP;
- compute exact cap-4 optimum via 625 zero-witness assignments;
- if `C_unrestricted < C_cap4`, serialize the first witness and stop the positive-discovery arm.

Positive tightness terminal:

`QG9_SUPPORT5_TIGHT_WITNESS_FOUND`

requires a proof-carrying unrestricted witness with at least one generator of support exactly 5 and an independently reconstructed cap-4 lower bound strictly above it.

## Stronger-theorem arm if no witness

Absence in a frozen finite search cannot prove cap4. Instead use the surviving irreducible skeletons to discover a **combined exchange** missed by QG-1.

The canonical proof treats non-coincidence SOLO moves and coincidence PAIR moves separately. A possible stronger move can combine:
- a non-zero-sum subset from `N_j0`;
- a non-zero-sum subset from `N_j1`;
- a subset of coincidence columns;

so their **joint five conserved coordinates** cancel even when none of the three components is individually zero-sum.

Required search/theorem programme:
1. enumerate every joint zero-sum-free `(N0,N1,C)` exceptional class pattern compatible with support 5;
2. test all semantics-preserving combined deletion masks and exact local cost changes against adversarial target letters/centrals;
3. classify whether every support-five irreducible pattern has a non-increasing combined move;
4. if yes, prove all-n support<=4 by lexicographic descent;
5. if not, extract a minimal algebraic obstruction and feed it back into the inverse-design witness generator.

Possible stronger terminals:
- `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT4_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT3_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Any stronger theorem must bind the full production R6I acceptance/cost semantics and independently replay the move inequalities; no inference from failure to find a witness.

## Search efficiency / exactness

The n=5 unrestricted DP remains the frozen 10-bit XOR DP. The cap-4 referee should memoize constrained local tables by `(qubit, forced-zero-mask, target letters, centrals)` so the 625 outer assignments do not require 625 independent full rebuilds.

A second exact implementation should either:
- formulate support counts directly in an augmented DP state and compare with the zero-witness result on a smaller panel; or
- use branch-and-bound over support-capped symplectic frame pairs on selected n=4 controls.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION harness:
- prospectively freezes the skeleton/template search;
- executes unrestricted + cap4 referees;
- independently reconstructs any strict witness/lower bound;
- if no witness, drives combined-exchange enumeration rather than declaring a theorem from search absence.

Native ORION-Q harness:
- maintains `TIGHT_WITNESS / STRONGER_THEOREM / SEARCH_NEGATIVE_ONLY / CANNOT_CHECK` as separate responsibility states;
- a cap4 strict gap is sufficient for tightness;
- finite search equality can never self-promote support4 theorem authority.

## Novelty boundary

Binary linear dependence, Davenport constants, support-capped dynamic programming and inverse design are donor mathematics/algorithms. Candidate contribution is only the exact tightness characterization or improved all-n normal form of this rank-2 shared-Tag quantum compilation grammar. No physical quantum-speedup claim follows.
