title: [ORION-QG QG-10] Certified interval regime geometry without an exact global referee
body:
Parent programme: #740
Motivating residual: wave-2 R6 — transfer ORION-QG to a third family where exhaustive/global exact DP is not available
Founding exact-geometry families: R6M shared-Tag TARE; SixLCU PREP/SELECT
Related automatic theorem infrastructure: #756 / PR #759

## Status

**SCALABILITY FRONTIER — replace exact optimum labels by proof-carrying upper/lower envelopes with an explicit unresolved region.**

ORION-QG wave 1 works because each studied family has an exact finite referee: unrestricted DP or exhaustive enumeration. That is scientifically clean but cannot be the final field definition; realistic quantum compilation families quickly make exact global optimization intractable.

QG-10 asks:

> Can compilation regime geometry be defined and prospectively certified when the true optimum is unavailable, using independently derived upper/lower bounds that prove regime membership only when intervals separate and otherwise return CANNOT_CHECK?

## Certified interval object

For an instance x and compilation family F, maintain a **cost interval**

`I_F(x) = [L_F(x), U_F(x)]`

where:
- `U_F` is the exact cost of a verified feasible witness;
- `L_F` is a proof-carrying lower bound valid for every member of F;
- both include the same frozen objective/access/resource coordinates.

For the unrestricted parent optimum `OPT`, maintain `[L_*, U_*]` where `U_*` is the best verified compilation found and `L_*` is a global relaxation/lower bound.

No midpoint or heuristic score has scientific authority.

## Interval regime logic

### Certified family optimality
F is certified globally optimal if

`U_F <= min_G L_G` and `U_F <= L_*`

where G ranges over all registered competing families not containing F. Equality/ties are retained explicitly.

### Certified strict trade
A trade family T strictly beats donor D if

`U_T < L_D`.

### Certified donor exactness
If donor D is a subfamily of unrestricted space and

`U_D == L_*`,

then D is globally exact without solving the unrestricted optimizer.

### Certified non-membership
If `L_F > U_*`, family F cannot contain an optimum.

### Unresolved band
If intervals overlap so none of the above conditions follows, terminal is `CANNOT_CHECK_INTERVAL_OVERLAP`. The system must not pick the smallest midpoint or best heuristic and call it a regime.

## Lower-bound library — donor first right of refusal

QG-10 does not claim lower-bound techniques themselves. Candidate sources:

1. **semantic relaxations:** drop coupling/placement constraints to obtain a cheaper superset problem;
2. **local/resource inequalities:** sum certified per-coordinate minima like R6N/R6S exchange bounds;
3. **LP/MILP/SMT relaxations:** use solver lower bounds / UNSAT depth certificates where available;
4. **cut/packing bounds:** routing/connectivity or Pauli-commutation lower bounds;
5. **dual bounds:** Lagrangian or convex-relaxation certificates;
6. **decomposition bounds:** solve blocks exactly while dropping inter-block coupling;
7. **complexity-theorem lower bounds:** parameter/gate-count minima when a theorem applies.

Every bound must declare exact assumptions and be independently reconstructible.

## Strong prior-art subtraction

Exact/optimal quantum compilation and solver-based optimality certification are established:
- SAT/SMT and exact synthesis methods certify optimal circuits on bounded instances;
- 2026 Auto-Stabilizer-Check iteratively invokes SMT and certifies nonexistence of depth-6 syndrome-extraction circuits for IBM BB-code instances while returning near-optimal solutions on timeout;
- formal compiler work routinely uses exact small-instance baselines and scalable heuristics.

Therefore QG-10 cannot claim novelty for branch-and-bound, lower bounds, SMT UNSAT certificates, exact synthesis, or approximation gaps.

The candidate contribution is only the **regime-geometry layer built from heterogeneous certified bounds**, with explicit anti-laundering rules and prospective regime forecasts under partial exact knowledge.

## Required calibration on existing exact families

Before touching a non-exact third family, hide exact ground truth and validate interval geometry on ORION-QG families where exact DP already exists.

### C1 — R6M TARE blind-referee calibration
For all 9,547 QG-5b compared instances:
- construct intervals using only registered lower-bound modules and feasible family witnesses;
- hide `C_DP` from the interval classifier;
- classify donor/split/borrow′/unresolved;
- only after classification reveal exact DP and score soundness.

Primary metrics:
- **false certification rate must be 0**;
- resolved fraction / coverage;
- interval width;
- regime precision conditional on certification;
- lower-bound compute cost.

### C2 — SixLCU calibration
Repeat on QG-4 exhaustive domains. Test whether the pairs-only predicate and family bounds yield certified membership without reading exact optimum.

### C3 — adversarial weakened bounds
Deliberately remove one lower-bound source; resolved fraction should fall, but false certification must remain zero. This distinguishes a sound CANNOT_CHECK system from one that fills evidence gaps with guesses.

## Third-family target

After calibration, choose a materially different quantum compilation/resource family for which:
- exact global optimum is unavailable at target size;
- at least two meaningful restricted families and one global lower bound exist;
- witness validity is efficiently checkable;
- objective/access semantics are exact enough for matched comparison.

Candidate classes to research, donor-first:
- larger LCU/block-encoding PREP/SELECT synthesis;
- Hamiltonian Pauli-rotation grouping/synthesis beyond exact enumeration;
- qLDPC syndrome-extraction scheduling where SMT supplies lower bounds/certificates but not always full optimum;
- hardware-constrained lattice-surgery/surface-code scheduling;
- large Paulihedral/ZX extraction choices with independent gate/depth lower bounds.

Selection must be prospectively frozen after donor review.

## Certified forecast object

A regime forecast may output only:

- `CERTIFIED_DONOR_EXACT`
- `CERTIFIED_TRADE_<id>`
- `CERTIFIED_FAMILY_NONOPTIMAL_<id>`
- `MULTIPLE_CERTIFIED_TIE`
- `CANNOT_CHECK_INTERVAL_OVERLAP`

and carries the exact interval endpoints/bound certificates that force the terminal.

## Active bound acquisition

When CANNOT_CHECK, ORION may choose an additional computation by value of information:
- tighten the global lower bound;
- optimize one family further to lower its upper bound;
- prove/refute a coupling constraint;
- split the instance into a regime-specific subproblem.

This uses ORION's existing epistemic computation layer; it is a research-cost policy, not part of the mathematical certification itself.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION harness:
- verifies every witness and lower-bound certificate independently;
- runs blind-ground-truth calibration;
- reconstructs interval-derived terminals.

Native ORION-Q harness:
- enforces non-overlap logic and CANNOT_CHECK;
- prevents heuristic incumbent scores from entering lower-bound fields;
- controls active bound acquisition under a frozen budget.

## Success terminals

Calibration success:
`QG10_CERTIFIED_INTERVAL_GEOMETRY_SOUND__ZERO_FALSE_CERTIFICATIONS_ON_EXACT_CALIBRATION`

Third-family positive:
`QG10_INTERVAL_REGIME_GEOMETRY_TRANSFERRED_BEYOND_EXACT_REFEREE`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG10_BOUNDS_TOO_WEAK__MOSTLY_CANNOT_CHECK`
- `QG10_FALSE_CERTIFICATION_FOUND`
- `QG10_THIRD_FAMILY_DONOR_OWNS_OBJECT`
- `QG10_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Publication significance

If successful, this removes the largest scalability objection to ORION-QG. Exact regime geometry becomes one end of a spectrum; at larger scale the framework still makes **sound regime statements with abstention**, rather than silently replacing the exact referee by an optimizer heuristic.

No physical quantum-speedup claim follows.

Compositional compilation is established:
- **qstack** (2026) provides compositional end-to-end FT quantum compilation through quantum/QEC/ISA layers and wraps classical callbacks;
- modular/verified compilation and direct refinements between open modules are established PL theory;
- modular quantum uncomputation/synthesis, modular compiler IRs, ScaffCC-style scalable modular compilation and current QRE pipelines are prior art.

Therefore QG-14 cannot claim novelty for compiler-pass composition, modular IRs, semantic refinement, or modular resource estimation.

Candidate contribution is only a **calculus for composing ORION-QG optimality/regime certificates**: normal-form families, parameter cells, interval bounds, obstruction certificates and explicit unresolved couplings.

## Component certificate

A component i exports a proof-carrying interface:

```text
RegimeInterface
semantic_input_contract
semantic_output_contract
admitted_information/access
resource_coordinates
objective_parameters
certified_region K_i
normal_form_family F_i
cost_expression / interval

certificate_obligations
latent_coupling_coordinates
CANNOT_CHECK_conditions
provenance/backend/compiler identity
```

The internal optimizer need not be exposed if the interface theorem is sufficient.

## C1 — separable composition theorem

For independent components with additive resources

`r_total = sum_i r_i`

and no shared constraints except typed semantic composition, prove:

- if each component theorem is applicable under the same global objective projection;
- each selected normal form is independently optimal for its component;
- component choices do not change another component's feasible set/resource map;

then the tuple of component-optimal normal forms is globally optimal for the product family and total cost is the sum of certified component costs.

This is elementary separable optimization and receives zero novelty credit; the scientific value is the machine-checked compiler interface and anti-coupling conditions.

## C2 — shared-budget composition

If components share a global budget/resource (ancilla pool, T factories, error budget, routing fabric, measurement channel), independent optimality may fail.

Represent coupling by explicit coordinates/constraints:

`H(r_1,...,r_m) <= 0`.

Possible certified strategies:
- Lagrange/dual prices convert shared constraints to component objective coefficients and use QG-8/QG-11 phase cells;
- finite budget allocation DP over component regime summaries;
- interval bounds from QG-10 where exact allocation is unavailable.

Any duality/DP mathematics is donor-owned. QG-14 must preserve exact conditions under which the composed certificate is valid.

## C3 — regime-boundary convolution

For components with piecewise-linear/polyhedral cost envelopes, compute the global parameter-space arrangement induced by all component boundaries plus shared-budget constraints.

Output cells contain:
- selected normal-form tuple;
- exact/interval total resource expression;
- active component boundary predicates;
- coupling certificate;
- distance/margin to nearest regime change.

The number of Cartesian cells may explode; exploit certificate arity/low-order obstruction structure where proven, but do not assume it generically.

## C4 — cross-component counterexample hunt

Actively construct cases where independently valid local regimes fail globally because of a hidden coupling:

- two components individually choose T-heavy low-qubit forms but jointly saturate magic-state factories;
- separate ancilla-minimal forms serialize a shared measurement bottleneck;
- local PREP/SELECT choices change global QSVT normalization/query count;
- block-encoding scaling changes the number/degree of later polynomial transforms;
- shared routing/layout causes a local support reduction to increase total communication;
- error-budget allocation changes code distances differently across components.

A minimal witness is a positive scientific result:

`QG14_LOCAL_REGIME_CERTIFICATES_NOT_COMPOSITIONALLY_SUFFICIENT__MISSING_COUPLING_<id>`.

It identifies a coordinate that must be added to RegimeInterface.

## C5 — first exact compositional calibration

Build a synthetic/exact two-component world from already solved ORION-QG families:

- component A: R6M TARE/QG-8 objective-phase theorem;
- component B: SixLCU/QG-12 theorem or a second R6M instance;
- first arm strictly additive -> separable theorem must predict exact product optimum;
- second arm introduce one frozen shared resource coupling -> naive product must fail and coupling-aware calculus must recover exact optimum.

Use exact enumeration/DP as hidden referee only after composed prediction is frozen.

## C6 — real algorithmic vertical slice

After exact calibration, choose an actual algorithmic pipeline with at least two materially coupled compilation components, e.g.:
- LCU block encoding + qubitization/QSVT;
- PREP/SELECT + amplitude-amplification/query layer;
- Hamiltonian block encoding + FT factory/layout layer.

Freeze donor implementations and interface contracts first. Compare:
- monolithic best-known compiler/QRE;
- independent component regime selection;
- QG-14 coupling-aware composition.

Claim only the exact earned layer (logical/FT estimate, not observed speedup).

## C7 — incremental recomposition

A practical benefit of certificate composition should be **local invalidation**: when one component/backend/objective changes, only downstream regime interfaces whose assumptions depend on it reopen. Recompute affected cells rather than the entire monolithic optimization.

Measure:
- proof/certificate reuse fraction;
- recomputation cost;
- false stale-certificate rate (must be zero);
- agreement with full recomputation on calibration worlds.

Dynamic assurance/dependency invalidation are prior art; candidate value is the concrete compiler-regime composition semantics.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION harness:
- independently reconstructs component certificate applicability and composed cost/bounds;
- runs hidden monolithic referee on calibration worlds only after prediction;
- verifies counterexamples/coupling witnesses.

Native ORION-Q harness:

> What is the **minimal sufficient state** of a compilation problem for deciding the regime label or exact residual optimum, and how much larger is that state than the natural structural vocabulary?

### E_label — regime-label equivalence
`s ~_label t` iff for every admissible continuation/input suffix `z`, the final regime label is identical from `s+z` and `t+z`.

### E_value — optimal residual-value equivalence
`s ~_value t` iff for every admissible continuation `z`, the exact optimal residual cost differs by the same declared additive offset (or is exactly equal under a normalized convention).

## Status

**WAVE-3 ROBUSTNESS FRONTIER — quantify how far a proof-carrying compiler regime remains certified when objective coefficients, estimator parameters, or downstream stack assumptions vary.**

ORION-QG already has exact certificate cones in objective space, but it usually reports only `inside/outside` and keeps true global boundary sharpness OPEN. The missing object is a rigorous separation between:

1. **certificate margin** — distance from a point/set to the boundary of the currently proved sufficient region;
2. **true phase margin** — distance to an actual global change of optimal normal form/regime.

These are not interchangeable. A proof cone may be conservative. QG-21 must never call a certificate radius a true phase radius unless a separately verified sharpness/completeness argument closes the gap.

## Strong donor subtraction

Robust optimization, sensitivity analysis, parametric programming, uncertainty propagation, polyhedral distance calculations, dual norms, interval analysis, and robust control are donor mathematics. Piecewise-affine resource maps and critical regions are also established.

Candidate contribution is restricted to a **compiler-specific proof-carrying robustness certificate** that composes ORION-QG regime theorems with exact uncertainty sets and preserves the distinction between theorem applicability and the unknown true phase diagram.

## Q1 — exact certificate margin on QG-8 / QG-16

For a certified polyhedral regime

`K = { theta : A theta >= 0 }`,

fix an explicit normalization/gauge before any margin is reported (examples: `t_r=1` for the QG-8/QG-16 slices, or a declared norm-simplex when scale is physically meaningful).

For a point `theta0 in K`, compute exact rational facet slacks `s_i = a_i·theta0`. Under a declared perturbation norm `||.||`, the distance to facet i is

`rho_i = s_i / ||a_i||_*`,

where `||.||_*` is the donor dual norm. The certified point radius is `rho_cert = min_i rho_i` within the declared gauge/feasible coefficient domain.

Required first calibrations:
- QG-8 support<=2 cone `t_c >= 2 t_r`, `t_nc >= 2 t_r`;
- QG-16 full four-facet support1 certificate, preserving any separate `t_c<=t_nc` premise rather than silently assuming it;
- equality controls must return radius zero exactly.

All arithmetic used for theorem gates is exact rational/algebraic where possible. Floating distances are display-only unless an independently certified interval encloses them.

## Q2 — robust uncertainty sets, not just points

Let `Theta` be a frozen uncertainty set for objective coefficients (box, simplex, rational polytope, or finite union of certified cells).

A normal-form theorem is robustly valid on Theta only if

`Theta subseteq K`.

For convex rational polytopes and linear certificate inequalities, verify containment exactly by vertex/facet optimization or LP certificates. For boxes, compute worst facet margin analytically.

Outputs:
- minimum certificate slack over Theta;
- active worst-case facet and witness point;
- maximal uniform box/polytope expansion that remains inside the certificate;
- exact CANNOT_CHECK if the uncertainty representation cannot be certified.

No midpoint or nominal-point substitution may authorize robust validity.

## Q3 — witness-side upper bounds on the true margin

Use QG-17 and other exact outside-cone witnesses to bound the unknown true phase boundary from the opposite side.

For a verified pair of feasible configurations with resource difference `d`, the tie surface is

`d·theta = 0`.

If one side is globally certified support1 and the other has an exact strict support2-vs-cap1 witness, then along a frozen one-dimensional path or affine slice these two facts bracket a true transition. Distinguish:
- lower bound from theorem applicability;
- upper bound from explicit globally discriminating witness;
- exact boundary only if the brackets coincide or a complete phase argument proves no intervening regime.

QG-17's finite witness hyperplanes are natural first controls, but QG-21 may not generalize them beyond their verified objectives/slices.

## Q4 — sensitivity tubes along hardware/stack trajectories

A practical compiler objective often comes from a downstream resource model. For an affine FT map

`r_F = A r_S + b`, final objective `lambda·r_F` induces structural coefficients `theta=A^T lambda`.

Given uncertainty in lambda, A, or both:
- propagate a proof-carrying enclosure for the induced theta set;
- certify the entire enclosure lies in a structural QG cone before transferring the normal-form theorem;
- report the nearest stack-parameter perturbation that can leave the certified cell.

This is a QG-11/QG-21 interface. The affine mathematics is donor-owned. If code distance, factory count, routing, or scheduling creates a piecewise/nonseparable map, split into verified cells or return `STACK_NONLINEARITY_CANNOT_CERTIFY_SINGLE_RADIUS`.

## Q5 — compositional robustness

For QG-14 component interfaces, carry not only a regime label but a **margin/assumption budget**:

- component certificate region K_i;
- current parameter/uncertainty set Theta_i;
- distance to local invalidation;
- latent/shared coupling assumptions;
- dependency edges indicating which downstream certificates reopen when a margin is crossed.

Under strictly separable composition, the global certified radius is limited by the first component certificate to fail after the declared parameter map. Under shared-budget coupling, recompute the coupled feasible parameter region; `min(local radii)` is not automatically valid.

A counterexample in which all local margins are positive but a hidden coupling causes a global regime flip is a strong positive result because it identifies a missing coupling coordinate.

## Q6 — prospective drift forecast

After calibration, freeze a parameter trajectory or uncertainty expansion before opening the full optimizer/estimator result.

Examples:
- slowly vary `t_tag/t_r` across a QG-16 facet;
- vary a factory/runtime coefficient in a QG-11 affine or piecewise-affine cell;

- the first point at which certificate authority must stop;
- if a sharpness witness exists, a bracket for the first true regime change.

Score false continuation of authority as a hard failure. Conservative early abstention is allowed and measured.

## Q7 — robustness profile, not one scalar when anisotropic

A single norm radius can hide highly anisotropic phase geometry. Also serialize:
- exact per-facet slacks;
- directional radii for declared scientifically meaningful coefficient directions;
- active-facet changes along paths;
- uncertainty-set volume/coverage only as a secondary descriptive metric.

The primary scientific object remains the exact certificate region plus its scope, not a visually convenient scalar.

`U_aux = supp(Tag) union all frame-support / phantom-home coordinates`

has cardinality at most six. (For A/C, frame support is on Tag coordinates; for P, the only extra coordinate is its one Tag-free home.)

Outside `U_aux`, every frame and Tag letter is identity. Therefore Restore letters equal the target letters there, and the F3 contribution of a spectator coordinate is fixed once the global target-permutation tuple is fixed.

This suggests a stronger exact representation in **column-count space** rather than word/order space.

For a fixed matching, each qubit column is one type

`t in Sigma = {I,X,Y,Z}^6`, `|Sigma|=4096`.

Let `N_t` be the number of physical qubits with type t. The vector

`N=(N_t)_{t in Sigma} in N^4096`

is the Parikh/histogram image of the six-target instance.

Simultaneously permuting physical qubit coordinates does not change Pauli weights, symplectic products, the F3 rule, Tag/frame feasibility or the frozen unit objective. QG-26 must machine-bind this permutation invariance rather than assume it from terminology.

For each of the 8 target-permutation tuples `pi`, define the exact linear spectator baseline

`B_pi(N) = sum_t N_t * b_pi(t)`,

`N_t >= m_tau(t)` for every t used by tau.

QG-26 earns, for every valid fixed-matching histogram `N in N^4096`,

`C_DP(N) = min_{tau feasible} [B_{pi(tau)}(N) + K_tau]`,

with an optimum whose nontrivial auxiliary letters occupy at most six physical columns. There are 8 target-permutation baselines, collapsing in QG-26 to 4 exact vectors.

This implies the auxiliary optimization is a finite **defect correction** on top of an extensive spectator/bulk baseline.

## Q1 — universal all-n defect band

Define

`B_min(N) = min_pi B_pi(N)`.

For any QG-23-normalized accepted template with `k<=6` active columns:
- its structural frame/Tag term, including the frozen `-18` offset, is at least 2 because all six frames are nonzero and the shared Tag has support at least 1;
- each active column replaces one spectator two-branch F3 baseline in `[0,6]` with another two-branch F3 value in `[0,6]`, so its local correction lies in `[-6,+6]`.

Hence every accepted normalized template obeys

`K_tau >= 2 - 6*k >= -34`.

Therefore

`C_DP(N) >= B_min(N) - 34`.

For the upper bound, choose a target-permutation pi attaining `B_min(N)` and any physical target column type present in N. On that one coordinate use any of the exact 48 feasible one-qubit shared-label frame/Tag rows from QG-24/QG-26; use identity auxiliary letters everywhere else. The one-active structural term is exactly 2 and its F3 correction is at most +6. Therefore

`C_DP(N) <= B_min(N) + 8`.

Frozen candidate band:

`B_min(N)-34 <= C_DP(N) <= B_min(N)+8`

for every valid fixed-matching TARE histogram and every physical n.

The constants are deliberately crude universal bounds, not claimed sharp. A successor may tighten them only prospectively.

## Q2 — vanishing auxiliary density / thermodynamic limit

For any sequence of valid histograms `N^(m)` with total qubit count `n_m=sum_t N_t^(m) -> infinity` and empirical frequencies

`p_t = lim_m N_t^(m)/n_m`

existing componentwise, divide the Q1 band by `n_m` to obtain

`C_DP(N^(m))/n_m -> min_pi sum_t p_t b_pi(t)`.

Thus the exact asymptotic cost density is determined solely by the finite set of spectator baseline linear forms; all optimized frame/Tag structure is subextensive `O(1)`.

This may be called a **compiler thermodynamic-limit / bulk-density theorem**, not a physical thermodynamic phase transition.

## Q3 — exact scaling rays are eventually affine

Fix a valid integer histogram motif `h` such that every one of the six target components is nonzero somewhere in h. Let

`N(k)=k h`, `k>=1`.

By QG-26, every finite template tau is either:
- never feasible on the ray because it requires a column type t with `h_t=0`; or
- feasible for all `k >= K_tau = max_t ceil(m_tau(t)/h_t)` over its used types.

Whenever feasible,

`C_tau(kh)=k B_pi(h)+K_tau_const`.

The lower envelope of finitely many affine functions is eventually one affine function (or several identical/tied functions). Therefore there exist exact integers `K>=1`, slope `s` and intercept `q` such that

`C_DP(kh)=k*s+q` for every `k>=K`.

Moreover, because for every target permutation pi and every target type present in h there exists a one-active feasible shared-label template, the asymptotic slope is exactly

`s = min_pi B_pi(h)`.

So QG-27 strengthens the generic QG-25 expectation from eventual affine-periodicity to **eventual exact affinity with period 1** on pure repetition rays.

## Q4 — asymptotic count-space phase cells

For normalized frequency vectors p, define the four distinct QG-26 bulk forms `beta_r(p)` corresponding to the four distinct spectator baseline vectors.

The asymptotic density is

`e(p)=min_r beta_r(p)`.

Therefore the frequency simplex is partitioned by a finite normal-fan-like arrangement of exact linear tie hyperplanes into **bulk compiler phase cells**. These are asymptotic TARE cost-density mechanisms only.

**PROSPECTIVE EXACT SYMMETRY-QUOTIENT THEOREM — freeze before execution.**

QG-26 proves that, for a fixed matching, exact all-n TARE cost depends only on the 4096-dimensional histogram of six-target local Pauli-column types

`t in {I,X,Y,Z}^6`.

The phase-free one-qubit Pauli algebra is `F_2^2`. Its full automorphism group is

`GL(2,2) ~= S_3`,

which fixes I and permutes X,Y,Z. The frozen TARE grammar uses only quantities invariant/equivariant under this automorphism: local multiplication, symplectic anticommutation, nonidentity weight, equality/nonidentity in F3, and sums/XORs of these local quantities.

Crucially, a different automorphism may be applied at **each physical qubit coordinate independently**, provided it is applied simultaneously to all six target letters and every local frame/Tag letter at that coordinate. This is a local-Clifford conjugation symmetry of the abstract cost/feasibility problem.

## Q1 — complete local equivariance

Enumerate all 6 automorphisms phi of `{I,X,Y,Z}` fixing I and permuting X,Y,Z. Require for every phi and every local letters:
- `phi(local_mul(a,b)) = local_mul(phi(a),phi(b))` for all 16 pairs;
- `local_symp(phi(a),phi(b)) = local_symp(a,b)` for all 16 pairs;
- `local_wt(phi(a)) = local_wt(a)` for all 4 letters;
- `F3(phi(a),phi(b),phi(c)) = F3(a,b,c)` for all 64 triples.

Production binds these independently reconstructed identities to frozen R6M tables. Generic ORION rebuilds `F_2^2` independently.

## Q2 — exact orbit census on target-column alphabet

Let S3 act diagonally on the six entries of one target-column type.

Burnside fixed sets are frozen falsifiable targets:
- identity: `4^6 = 4096` fixed types;
- each of the 3 transpositions of X/Y/Z fixes exactly I plus one nonidentity letter, hence `2^6 = 64` types;
- each of the 2 three-cycles fixes only I, hence `1^6 = 1` type.

Therefore expected orbit count:

`(4096 + 3*64 + 2*1)/6 = 715`.

Enumerate the complete 4096 types and require exact orbit-size distribution:
- 1 orbit of size 1;
- 63 orbits of size 3;
- 651 orbits of size 6.

Every type receives a deterministic canonical representative, lexicographically minimum in its orbit.

## Q3 — independent-coordinate symmetry and 715-count sufficient statistic

Because the S3 automorphism can be chosen independently per physical coordinate, every n-qubit target instance can be transformed cost-preservingly so that each qubit column is its canonical orbit representative.

Thus if `M_o` is the total number of columns belonging to orbit o, the 715-vector

`M=(M_o)`

is an exact sufficient statistic: any two valid target instances with the same 715 orbit-count vector have the same frozen exact optimum.

This is stronger than merely saying the 4096 histogram is invariant under one global S3 action.

Block permutations and swaps of the two target strings inside each block are only **global** relabelings of whole target strings. They cannot be chosen independently at each physical coordinate.

QG-28 V1 must explicitly reject the tempting but invalid step of aggregating the 4096 column types under an independently applied block/branch-position group. Native ORION-Q must keep `INDEPENDENT_POSITION_RELABEL_PER_COLUMN=false`.

For each QG-26 active template, independently transform each active coordinate's target type to its canonical S3 orbit representative and apply the same local automorphism to that coordinate's six frame letters and Tag letter. Equivariance preserves:
- acceptance;
- local structural support cost;
- Restore/F3 correction;
- multiplicity.

Hence exact all-n cost admits a finite guarded min-affine representation directly on `N^715`.

- lifting each quotient vector back to 4096 entries using orbit membership reproduces the parent QG-26 vector exactly.

The histogram above counts orbits, not weighted alphabet multiplicity; do not confuse it with QG-26's 4096-entry coefficient histogram.

RuntimeError: local harness capability failed: <error>

`_run_local` requests the PYTHON capability with a hardcoded ceiling:

```python
request = workspace.get_or_create_request(
    capability="PYTHON", payload={"code": code, "cwd": ".", "timeout": 120}
)
```

and the code it runs is `research/extensions/orion-qg/qg3_stage1_select.py`.

Evidence:

- observed run: step started `2026-08-22T17:06:36Z`, raised at `17:08:37Z` —
  **121 s**, i.e. the 120 s ceiling plus overhead;
- running `qg3_stage1_select.py` directly on a local machine also exceeds 120 s.
  The exact runtime was **not** measured — two attempts were killed at the
  120 s mark — so the only firm statement is `> 120 s`.

## Why it was not seen before

The workflow sets

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: orion-qg-qg3-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

and every other recent run is on `claude/orion-harness-verification-b17qdj` with

by the QG-3 harness; they match the workflow's `paths:` trigger and nothing more.

stage-1 runtime, or reduce stage-1's work. Whichever is chosen, the actual
runtime of `qg3_stage1_select.py` should be measured and recorded so the ceiling
is set from evidence rather than guessed.

forecast workflow: it is what kept this defect invisible.

title: [ORION-QG QG-37] One-corruption-resilient indexed probe identification
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Earned structural parents: QG-32 #911 (joint summaries + certified fixed separator), QG-32c #928 (exact universal noiseless fixed minimum 5), QG-34 #924 (exact noiseless adaptive minimax depth 3).
Fair noiseless fixed baseline: QG-35 #932 (pending exact accepted receipt at registration time).
Fair comparison: QG-36 #933 (frozen receipt composition, pending QG-35).

Donor areas to subtract: minimum test cover / distinguishing sensor placement; branch-and-bound test cover; active probing/adaptive diagnosis; separating systems and Ulam/Rényi liar games; noisy adaptive group testing; error-correcting codes.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE ROBUST-OBSERVATION FRONTIER. NO ROBUST CARDINALITY OR ADVANTAGE IS PREDICTED.**

All earned QG-32/QG-34 observation results assume exact probe answers. QG-37 asks a new robustness question:

> How many indexed structural probes are required so that the 715-way local-response identity remains uniquely recoverable after the joint bulk+spectrum summary is known, even if **one selected probe response is adversarially corrupted**?

This is an ORION-Q research-control robustness question, not a hardware-noise or quantum-measurement claim.

## Q1 — exact one-corruption fixed-code criterion

For a fixed selected probe set `P`, each orbit `o` has a multivalued response word `K_P(o)`.

Under at most one adversarially corrupted coordinate, unique decoding is possible iff every pair of distinct relevant orbit identities has Hamming distance at least 3:

`d_H(K_P(a), K_P(b)) >= 3`.

For one known joint summary class `S`, define `R1(S)` as the minimum cardinality of a fixed probe set selected after `S` is known such that every pair in `S` is distinguished on at least three selected probes.

Define `R1_* = max_S R1(S)`.

Also define `R1_universal` for one fixed probe set that works across all 92 joint classes. Keep the class-conditioned and universal quantities separate.

## Q2 — exact multicover formulation

For every orbit pair, probe `p` contributes one unit iff its exact responses differ. The robust fixed problem is therefore a minimum **3-cover of every pair**, not ordinary test cover.

Production exact method may use:
- pair-demand branch-and-bound with residual demand 0..3;
- safe dominance only when a probe's full pair-incidence dominates another's incidence;
- lower bounds from total residual demand / maximum marginal contribution and per-pair remaining candidates;
- QG-32/QG-35 noiseless solutions only as lower bounds or constructive seeds where logically valid, never as robust authority.

Generic ORION must use a different exact formulation, e.g. binary ILP / SAT / bounded exhaustive cardinality with constraints `sum_{p distinguishes pair} x_p >= 3`.

## Q3 — decoding certificate

For every positive robust result, serialize and verify:
- selected probe indices;
- minimum pairwise response-word Hamming distance;
- all pairs attaining the minimum distance;
- an exact nearest-codeword decoder or equivalent proof that every radius-1 corrupted word maps to at most one orbit within its known summary class.

A cardinality alone is insufficient.

## Q4 — robustness overhead

Only after QG-35 is exact may compare class-conditioned noiseless `F(S)` to robust `R1(S)`.

Define per-class overhead `R1(S)-F(S)` and worst overhead, but do not interpret this as physical noise cost. It is redundancy required for one-error authority robustness in the structural-probe interface.

## Q5 — ORION-Q consequence

A GREEN result may authorize a domain-specific fail-closed rule:
- when one structural probe answer may be unreliable, do not use a noiseless distinguishing set as identity authority;
- require an exact radius-1 robust probe code / decoder, or escalate to richer state/referee.

This extends the QG-derived authority router from query scope to **evidence reliability scope**.

## Independent verification

Production:
- exact response matrix reconstruction;
- exact minimum 3-cover per class and universal variant where tractable;
- explicit decoder/distance certificate.

Generic ORION:
- independent F2^2/F3 reconstruction;
- separate exact optimization formulation;
- independently recompute all pairwise distances and radius-1 decoding uniqueness.

Native ORION-Q:
- authorize only one-corruption structural-probe identity robustness on the frozen observation problem.

Workflow must require deterministic replay and reject a self-consistent tamper that lowers a claimed pairwise distance / removes a redundancy probe while recomputing result digest.

## Hard boundaries

Always false:
- hardware measurement noise model;
- stochastic physical error rate;
- fault-tolerant quantum-computing threshold claim;
- full finite-n optimum probes;
- generic coding/separating-system novelty;
- physical quantum advantage.

## Honest terminals

- `QG37_EXACT_ONE_CORRUPTION_FIXED_PROBE_CODE_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG37_ROBUST_FIXED_UPPER_BOUND_ONLY`
- `QG37_ROBUST_CODE_INFEASIBLE_IN_FROZEN_PROBE_LIBRARY`
- `QG37_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Donor subtraction

Minimum test cover, separating systems, error-correcting Hamming-distance criteria, adaptive diagnosis and noisy group testing are established donor ideas. Candidate value is only the exact TARE/QG-32 response-code geometry and its scoped ORION-Q evidence-reliability consequence.
